## 1. Project Snapshot (never delete this)
- **What we're building:** A custom booking + salon management platform for Looks Smart Beauty Salon.
  Public marketing site + online booking + full admin dashboard (bookings, POS, CRM, CMS, reports).
- **Why:** The old version ran on Base44 (no-code) — features were incomplete and there was no control.
  Now it's built from scratch, security-first.
- **Stack:** Laravel 12 (PHP 8.2 locally / 8.3 target for staging-prod — see Decisions #9, #12) +
  Inertia v2 (`inertiajs/inertia-laravel` v3) + React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 7 + Tailwind v4 + shadcn-style
  primitives + MySQL 8 (locally: MariaDB 10.4.32 via XAMPP — below the Brief's own 10.11+ floor, accepted
  as tech debt, see Decision #11 / §10 #8) + Redis 7 (staging/production; **not used locally** — see
  Decision #10 and §10 #6) + Horizon. Details in `00-PROJECT-BRIEF.md`.
- **Local dev environment (deviates from Brief §1's "Laravel Sail" line — see Decision #8):** native
  XAMPP (PHP 8.2.12, MariaDB) on Windows, no Docker. `php artisan serve` + `npm run dev`, no containers.
- **Non-negotiables:** tight security (Brief §5), SSR SEO, Lighthouse ≥95, fully responsive,
  minimal-luxury UI with motion/glass/smooth-scroll.

- **[Phase 8] Notification channels + real-time booking broadcasts** — implemented branded mail layouts and a shared notification flow across `BookingConfirmed`, `BookingCancelled`, `BookingRescheduled`, `ReviewRequest`, `BirthdayOffer`, and `StaffDailySchedule`; created `BookingCreated`/`BookingCancelled`/`BookingRescheduled` event classes and dispatched them from the booking actions; added `App\Channels\SmsChannel` and `App\Channels\WhatsappChannel` using Laravel's `Http` facade for Twilio requests with fail-closed behavior when credentials are empty; verified by running `php artisan test tests/Feature/Booking/Phase8NotificationsTest.php` — `8 passed (15 assertions)`.

- **[Phase 10 — sub-step 4] Site Settings Engine & management UI** — confirmed via `AskUserQuestion`
  before building: all 9 Brief-listed settings categories (Business Info, Operating Hours, Booking
  Rules, Taxes & Fees, Payment Gateway Toggles, Email/SMS/WhatsApp Credentials, Google Maps/Analytics,
  SEO Defaults, Security Configs) would be genuinely built and stored, with the caveat — documented
  in code and here, not hidden — that Payments/Integrations/Security have no live consumer yet
  (Phase 12+ builds real payment processing; Mail/Twilio/Google still read `.env`/`config()` directly).
  Built `App\Services\SettingService` — the single call site for every settings read/write, with a
  `SCHEMA` allowlist (29 keys across 6 groups: `business`/`booking`/`payments`/`integrations`/`seo`/
  `security`) declaring each key's type and whether it's encrypted. Secrets (Stripe/Twilio/Google API
  keys) are `Crypt::encryptString()`'d before storage and the service only ever returns a `MASK`
  sentinel for them to the UI — `maskedGroup()` never leaks a real secret value back to the browser.
  Submitting a blank value for an encrypted field is treated as "leave unchanged" (skipped, not
  cleared) — a blank non-secret field IS saved as empty, a deliberate distinction. Writing through
  `SettingService::set()` reuses `Setting::updateOrCreate()`, so the Phase 6 model-event cache-busting
  (`Cache::forget("setting:{$key}")` on save) applies automatically with no new cache-invalidation code
  needed — confirmed genuinely busted-and-repopulated in a real test, not assumed. **Found and fixed a
  real bug during testing, not shipped silently**: the first `SettingController::updateGroup()`
  implementation declared Laravel validation rules keyed as `"settings.{$key}"` (e.g.
  `settings.business.name`) — but Laravel's validator parses dots in rule keys as NESTED ARRAY PATHS
  (`settings → business → name`), not as a flat key that itself contains a literal dot. Every write
  silently validated against the wrong (nonexistent) input shape, `$request->validate()` returned an
  empty `settings` array, and the endpoint appeared to succeed (a real `302` redirect, no error) while
  writing nothing — caught by writing the cache-busting test, not by reading the code. Diagnosed by
  isolating `SettingService::updateGroup()` (worked correctly in isolation) then dumping the actual
  validated payload from inside the real HTTP request (came back `[]`). Fixed by replacing the
  Laravel-rule-array approach with hand-built validation in a new `validateGroupPayload()` method that
  throws a manually-constructed `ValidationException` — sidesteps the dot-collision entirely while
  still producing the same `settings.{key}` session-error keys the UI expects. `SettingController` also
  has `updateHours()` (bulk `BusinessHour` upsert — the actual live-consumed Operating Hours table from
  Phase 2, not a `Setting` row) and `uploadLogo()`/`uploadFavicon()` (via `SecureUploadService::
  storePublicImage()`). All write endpoints authorize via the pre-existing `SettingPolicy`
  (`settings.manage` — genuinely super-admin-only per the Phase 3 seeder, `admin` has `settings.view`
  only per Brief §2 — verified with a real 403 in the test suite, not just assumed from reading the
  policy). Replaced `Admin/Settings.tsx` placeholder with a hand-rolled 6-tab `Settings/Index.tsx`
  (General/Business Hours/Booking Rules/Payments & Taxes/Integrations/SEO & Security — no new tab
  library, matching the project's existing pattern of hand-rolling simple UI rather than adding Radix
  primitives for straightforward cases) — each tab's form independently submits to its own group
  endpoint via Inertia's `useForm().transform()` (to remap short local field names back to full
  `group.key` schema paths before sending), with `sonner` toasts confirming "cache cleared" on save.
  Added `tests/Feature/Admin/SettingControllerTest.php` — 7 tests: `settings.view` can read but not
  write (403), `settings.manage` required to even view, a real cache-bust-and-repopulate assertion,
  encryption + masking + blank-means-unchanged for a secret field, real per-field validation errors
  for both an invalid type and an unknown key, and a real Operating Hours bulk update. Verification:
  `php artisan test tests/Feature/Admin/SettingControllerTest.php` — `7 passed (25 assertions)`;
  `npm run typecheck` — clean; `npm run lint` (0 warnings) — clean (fixed the same unassociated-`<label>`-
  around-`Switch` a11y pattern as sub-step 3, on the hours-table's "Closed" toggle); `./vendor/bin/pint
  --test` — clean; live-verified `GET /admin/settings` against the real running server (unauthenticated
  → 302 to login). Full-suite `php artisan test` result recorded in §4 below.

- **[Phase 12 — sub-step 1] Advanced Financial Analytics & POS Reporting** — confirmed by grepping
  the codebase (same check already applied to `sales`/`payments` in Phase 11 sub-step 4's Customer
  360 work) that neither `Sale`/`SaleItem` nor `Payment` has ever been written to anywhere in the
  app — POS transaction recording is real schema (Phase 2) but a later Phase 12 sub-step's job, not
  this one. So **completed `bookings` are the primary revenue source** here — real, populated,
  already-tested data from Phase 7 — not the empty POS tables. Revenue math is derived directly from
  `PriceQuoteService`'s own formula (`total = (subtotal − discount) + tax`), confirmed algebraically
  and then proven with an exact-arithmetic test (two bookings with hand-picked discount/tax/total
  values, asserting `gross_revenue`/`net_revenue`/`discounts`/`tax` down to the cent):
  `net revenue = SUM(total) − SUM(tax)` (post-discount, pre-tax — what `subtotal − discount` actually
  equals) and `gross revenue = net revenue + SUM(discount)` (reconstructing `subtotal`, which
  `bookings` doesn't store directly). **Deliberately did NOT label a KPI "Net Profit"** — there is no
  cost/expense data anywhere in this schema to compute real profit, only post-discount revenue; the
  card is honestly labeled "Net Revenue" instead of claiming a number the app can't actually back.
  **Payment method split queries the real `payments` table with a correct, real query** — it returns
  empty on this dataset (no producer yet), same "real query, no producer yet" pattern already used

  permission — `admin`/`super-admin` only, per the Phase 3 seeder) with a shared `resolveRange()`
  (today/this_week/this_month/custom) and `buildReport()` used by all three actions, so the numbers
  on-screen, in the CSV, and in the PDF can never drift apart from each other. `exportCsv` streams a
  real CSV via `response()->streamDownload()` + `fputcsv()` (not maatwebsite/excel — this is flat
  tabular data with no need for that package's spreadsheet-specific features); `exportPdf` renders a
  new `resources/views/reports/financial-pdf.blade.php` through dompdf. Top services (via
  `BookingItem.price_snapshot`, grouped by service) and staff performance (via `Booking.staff_id` +

  fabricated one, even though nothing currently pays it out) both come from real, populated Phase 7

  payment-method pie chart (with an honest empty state), a top-5-services bar chart, a staff

  (`status`/`open`/`addCash`/`removeCash`/`close`/`zReport`) — deliberately scoped to the
  register/shift/reconciliation layer only, not a sale-ringing cart/checkout terminal, since nothing
  in that endpoint list concerns line items or carts (that remains a later Phase 12 sub-step, once
  `Sale`/`SaleItem`/`Payment` get a real producer). `open()` enforces a single-drawer invariant
  (`abort_if(CashRegisterShift::open()->exists(), 409, ...)`); `addCash`/`removeCash`/`close` all
  guard against acting on an already-closed shift; `removeCash()` additionally refuses to withdraw
  more than `expectedCashTotal()` currently holds, so the drawer can never go negative. Expected cash
  is computed as opening float + deposits − withdrawals + succeeded `cash`-method `Payment` rows
  recorded during the shift's `[opened_at, closed_at ?? now()]` window (`paymentBreakdown()` groups
  real `Payment.method` values with a live query, not a hardcoded method list — mirroring the
  "real query, no producer yet" pattern from Phase 12 sub-step 1's payment-split chart, now with real
  producers once the checkout sub-step lands). `close()` persists `closing_float`/`expected_total`/
  `counted_total`/signed `variance` and flips `status` to closed. `zReport()` returns JSON (not an
  Inertia page, matching the Leads/Messages/Reviews/Media-Library detail-endpoint pattern from Phase
  11/10) so the printable report can be re-fetched on demand, including the full movement list and
  payment-method breakdown. **Caught and fixed a real operator-precedence bug before writing any
  tests**: `(float) $this->paymentBreakdown($shift)['cash'] ?? 0` binds the cast to the array access
  first, so a missing `'cash'` key would warn before the cast ever ran and the `?? 0` was dead code —
  split into `$breakdown = $this->paymentBreakdown($shift); $cashPayments = (float) ($breakdown['cash']
  ?? 0);`. Built `Admin/POS/Index.tsx` (register status banner with open/close/add-cash/remove-cash
  modals, recent-shifts table) and `Admin/POS/RegisterClose.tsx` (exports `RegisterCloseDialog`, a
  component, not a routed page) — a client-side denomination calculator
  (`[100,50,20,10,5,1,0.25,0.1,0.05]`) sums to a single `counted_total` for the literal "counted cash
  breakdown input" UI ask without needing new schema (the DB only ever stores one counted figure), an
  expected-vs-counted-vs-variance summary card, and a printable Z-Report view with a Print button.
  Deleted the old `Admin/Pos.tsx` placeholder and its route; wired all 6 new routes in
  `routes/admin.php`. Wrote `tests/Feature/Admin/PosRegisterControllerTest.php` — 8 tests: authorization
  (`pos.sell`/`pos.refund` required), opening a register with a float, refusing a second concurrent
  open (409), cash deposit/withdrawal tracking against the float (asserted via the real
  `current_expected_cash` Inertia prop), refusing to over-withdraw (422), exact expected-cash math
  including a real succeeded `cash` payment while correctly excluding a `card` payment and a `pending`
  `cash` payment, closing with the correct signed variance, refusing to close an already-closed shift
  (409), and the Z-Report only being available once closed (409 while open, `assertOk()` after).
  **Caught and fixed a real test-side `MassAssignmentException`**: the expected-cash test originally
  passed `'created_at' => now()` into `Payment::create()`, but `created_at` isn't in `Payment`'s
  `$fillable` — the app's Phase 4 `preventSilentlyDiscardingAttributes` control correctly threw rather
  than silently drop it; fixed by removing the redundant timestamp (the shift's `opened_at` was already
  set an hour in the past, so the payment's default auto-timestamp naturally falls inside the window).
  All 8 passed (30 assertions) after that fix. Verification: `npm run typecheck` — clean; `npm run lint`
  — found and fixed one real `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning (wrapped `loadReport` in
  `React.useCallback`), then clean; `./vendor/bin/pint --test` — clean; `npm run build` — succeeds;
  live-verified `GET /admin/pos` returns a `302` unauthenticated redirect against the real running

- **[Phase 12 — sub-step 3] POS Checkout Engine, Real Sale/Payment Recording & Dev Auth Bypass** — the
  first real producer for `Sale`/`SaleItem`/`Payment`: sub-step 1's payment-split chart and sub-step
  2's `paymentBreakdown()` have both been running real, correct queries against permanently-empty
  tables until now. Added `PriceQuoteService::quoteCart()` — `quote()` (the booking engine's existing
  pricer) assumes exactly one unit of each service id in its input array, which a POS cart with real
  quantities can't use, so this is a second public method rather than a breaking change to `quote()`'s
  signature; it reuses the exact same private deal-matching/limit/applicability logic
  (`dealApplies()`/`dealWithinLimits()`/`assertDealUsable()`/`calculateDiscount()`) so a coupon behaves
  identically whether it's redeemed through a booking or the register, and reuses the same
  `booking.tax_rate` setting (the app's only tax-rate concept — there is no separate POS tax setting to
  invent). **Found and fixed a real, pre-existing schema gap**: `deal_redemptions` (Phase 2) only ever
  had a `booking_id`, so a coupon applied at checkout would never count toward
  `Deal.usage_limit`/`per_user_limit` — confirmed by grep before writing any code, same discipline as
  every prior "is this table actually written to" check this session. Added a nullable
  `deal_redemptions.sale_id` (migration `2026_09_03_170054`), a `Sale::dealRedemptions()` relation, and
  a dedicated test proving a `per_user_limit=1` coupon redeemed once via POS is genuinely rejected on a
  second POS attempt by the same customer — proof the fix actually feeds the shared limit-checking
  code, not just that the column exists. **Confirmed via `AskUserQuestion`** before writing any money
  code: Loyalty Points is a brand-new real payment method (`customer_profiles.loyalty_points`, Phase 2,
  had never been spent or earned anywhere in the app) — the user chose a fixed, documented 100-points-
  per-dollar rate over a new configurable Setting, so no Settings-module changes were needed. Built
  `PosCheckoutController`: `terminal()` (redirects to the register page if none is open; accepts an
  optional `?booking_id=` for a future "check out this appointment" deep link — the Bookings admin
  page is still a Phase 5 placeholder shell with no such button yet, so this is forward-compatible
  plumbing, not a fabricated feature), `searchServices`/`searchCustomers` (reusing the exact
  name/email/phone `whereHas('customerProfile')` search pattern from Phase 11 sub-step 4's Customer
  360), `applyCoupon` (doubles as the terminal's live, authoritative pricing preview — called on every
  cart change whether or not a coupon is present, exactly the same `quoteCart()` call `checkout()`
  itself makes, so the number on screen is never a client approximation), and `checkout()`. `checkout()`
  re-derives the ENTIRE price server-side from the submitted cart + coupon code — no `total`/`subtotal`/
  `tax` field is ever accepted from the client (Brief §4: "price calculation server-side ONLY"), then
  requires `sum(payments[].amount)` to match that total exactly before persisting anything. A loyalty-
  points payment locks the customer's `CustomerProfile` row (`lockForUpdate()`) and re-verifies the
  balance inside the same transaction as the decrement, closing the same class of double-spend race
  this project has guarded against since Phase 7's Redis slot locks and `CreateBookingAction`'s
  `lockForUpdate()`. A `booking_id` may only be linked if that booking is currently `checked_in`
  (matching `BookingStateMachine`'s own docblock, which explicitly anticipated "any later admin action
  (Phase 12+)" reusing it) — on success, `TransitionBookingStatusAction` (the existing single write
  path for booking status changes) moves it to `completed`, so the sale and the appointment's own
  status can never drift apart. Built `Admin/POS/Terminal.tsx` (search + category-tab service grid,
  cart drawer with quantity steppers/per-line staff picker/per-line discount input/customer lookup via
  a debounced `Popover` search/coupon input/live server-priced totals) and `Admin/POS/Payment` modal
  (method select, cash-tendered change calculator, card reference input, multi-line split payments,
  loyalty-points redemption showing the real available balance) plus `Admin/POS/Receipt.tsx`
  (`ReceiptDialog`, re-fetched by id from the real persisted sale — same "detail endpoint, never trust
  what the client just assembled" pattern as `RegisterClose.tsx`'s Z-Report — with a Print button).
  **Built the requested local-only dev-login**: `GET /admin/dev-login`, registered in `routes/web.php`
  only when `app()->environment('local')` is true AT ROUTE-REGISTRATION TIME (not just an in-handler

- **[Phase 13 — sub-step 2] Performance Optimization, Analytics Scripts & Accessibility/PWA-Lite** —
  added `integrations.google_tag_manager_id`/`google_site_verification` to `SettingService::SCHEMA`
  (`google_analytics_id` already existed but had zero consumers — now a real one) plus 2 new
  Settings-UI fields, with format-validated GTM/GA4 ids (`SettingController::validateGroupPayload()`)
  since both get embedded directly into an inline `<script>` template literal. Extended the `seo`
  shared Inertia prop (`HandleInertiaRequests`) with `gtmId`/`ga4Id`/`gscVerification` — always `null`,
  never a fabricated placeholder id, until actually configured — and added a `cspNonce` shared prop
  (the same per-request nonce `SecurityHeaders` already shares with Blade views). `SeoHead.tsx` now
  renders GA4's script pair, GTM's inline snippet, and the GSC `<meta>` tag, all reading from that one
  shared prop and all nonce'd — this app's CSP has no `unsafe-inline`, so an un-nonced inline script
  would simply be silently blocked, not "less secure." GTM's `<noscript>` body-tag fallback can't live
  in `SeoHead` at all (Inertia's `<Head>` only manages `<head>`) — added to `app.blade.php` instead,
  gated off `/admin*` the same way `SeoHead` itself is public-only (staff dashboard usage has no
  business in a customer-facing analytics property). **Real, necessary CSP work, not an afterthought**:
  GTM's snippet dynamically creates its own `<script>` tag from inside an already-nonce'd inline
  script — under CSP3 a nonce does not automatically propagate to a script a nonce'd script creates
  unless `'strict-dynamic'` is present (Google's own documented pattern for strict CSP + GTM) — so
  `SecurityHeaders::buildCsp()` now conditionally adds `'strict-dynamic'` plus the real Google domains
  to `script-src`/`frame-src`/`img-src`/`connect-src`, and ONLY when GTM or GA4 is actually configured;
  a site that never sets up analytics keeps the exact original locked-down policy. **Caught a real
  regression this introduced, before it shipped**: `buildCsp()` now reads `Setting::get()`, but a
  response header must never fail to generate — wrapped the read in a `try/catch` failing safe to the
  strict policy, since a header needed on literally every response can't be allowed to depend on the
  database being reachable (caught by `XssPayloadTest.php`, which doesn't migrate its DB, genuinely
  breaking on `/` until this fix). Built `SeoController::manifest()` (`/manifest.json`) — real
  `business.name`, real design-token colors (`--color-ivory`/`--color-accent-500` from
  `resources/css/app.css`, not placeholders), `favicon.ico` always included since it's the only icon
  asset this project actually ships, the real uploaded `business.logo_path` added only when it still
  exists on disk — logged honestly as not a proper multi-resolution PWA icon set, since there's no
  icon-generation pipeline in this project. Added `<link rel="preload" as="style">` for the Google
  Fonts stylesheet (the correct optimization for a Google-hosted stylesheet — its actual font file
  URLs are generated per-user-agent, not something safe to hardcode a preload for) and a real
  `theme-color` meta tag. **WebP conversion+fallback**: `SecureUploadService::storePublicImage()` now
  also writes a `.webp` sibling for every non-webp upload (the image is already decoded in memory from
  the existing re-encode step, so this is one extra `toWebp()` call, not a second decode) —
  `webpSiblingPath()` lets a consumer build a real `<picture>` without a separate "has webp" flag;
  `deletePublic()` cleans the sibling up too. Built a shared `Picture.tsx` (`<picture><source
  type="image/webp">` + `<img>` fallback, defaulting to `loading="lazy"`/`decoding="async"`) — a
  `<source>` pointing at a file that 404s breaks the image outright in WebP-capable browsers rather
  than falling through, so the server only ever sends a webp URL once
  `Storage::disk('public')->exists()` confirms it's real; applied to `MasonryGrid`/`BeforeAfterSlider`
  (Gallery page) via new `image_path_webp`/`pair_image_path_webp` fields on `PublicWebsiteController::
  gallery()`. Deliberately scoped to `SecureUploadService`-backed uploads only (Sliders/Gallery/
  branding) — Service/ServiceCategory images go through spatie/medialibrary's own separate pipeline,
  not retrofitted this pass, logged honestly rather than silently left half-covered. Audited every
  public `<img>` for `loading`/`decoding`: added `decoding="async"` everywhere `loading="lazy"` already
  existed (Home/Services/About/Blog/BlogDetail/MasonryGrid — the last now inherited from `Picture`),
  and `decoding="async"`/`fetchPriority="high"` (no `loading` — correctly eager) on the two genuine
  above-the-fold hero/cover images (ServiceDetail, BlogDetail). **Found and fixed 3 real accessibility
  bugs along the way, not part of the literal ask but caught while touching these exact files**: two
  meaningful blog-post thumbnails had `alt=""` (a plain-decorative marker) despite being the primary
  visual content of their own link — changed to the real post title; the gallery's keyboard-focusable
  "View" button overlay was only ever made visible by `:hover`, invisible to anyone tabbing to it —
  added `group-focus-within:opacity-100` alongside the existing `group-hover:` classes. Added a real
  focus trap to `Lightbox.tsx` (previously Escape/Arrow-key handling existed but nothing moved focus
  into the dialog on open, trapped Tab within it, or restored focus on close) and a "Skip to main
  content" link + `id="main-content"` on `PublicLayout.tsx` (previously absent — a WCAG 2.4.1 gap).
  Added `PerformanceAndA11yTest.php` — 9 tests: GTM/GA4/GSC shared correctly when configured and
  `null` when not, the CSP locked down by default and correctly loosened (with the real
  `'strict-dynamic'`/domain grants) only once configured, a real manifest.json structure test, the
  logo icon appearing only once it truly exists on disk (and not for a stale/deleted reference), and 2
  source-presence checks for `Picture.tsx`'s lazy/async defaults and the remaining raw-`<img>` pages —
  documented honestly as source checks, not DOM-rendering assertions, since this repo has no Vitest/

  **Live-verified via real SSR, including a genuine before/after of the CSP header itself**: seeded

- **[Phase 14 — sub-step 1] E2E Integration Audit, Security Hardening & Production Readiness** —
  **the most significant finding of the sub-step, found while writing the very test this sub-step
  itself asked for**: verifying "strict security headers across all HTTP responses" turned up a real,
  pre-existing, previously-undetected gap — `SecurityHeaders` (CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-
  Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy — every header Phase 4 built) was silently ABSENT from
  every response an exception produced, which in practice meant the single most common `/admin`
  request of all (an unauthenticated visit, redirected to `/login`) and every 404 shipped with zero
  security headers. Root cause, confirmed via a real middleware-pipeline introspection dump (not
  assumed from reading the code): `SecurityHeaders` was `append`ed to the `web` middleware group,
  which — confirmed empirically — resolves AFTER route-level middleware like `auth` for any route
  that declares its own (i.e. every `/admin/*` route); since `auth` *throws* `AuthenticationException`
  rather than returning a response when denying access, that exception unwound the request straight
  out of the pipeline without `SecurityHeaders` ever running at all. Two-part fix, each closing a
  distinct case: (1) `SecurityHeaders` is now `prepend`ed instead, ahead of route-level middleware,
  and its `handle()` now wraps `$next($request)` in a `try/catch`, rendering caught exceptions through
  the app's own `ExceptionHandler` (calling both `report()` and `render()`, so exceptions handled this
  way don't silently stop being logged) so the header-setting code always still runs on the resulting
  response — this covers any route that DID match but had its own middleware throw. (2) A path that
  matches NO route at all never reaches route middleware in the first place (Laravel's router raises
  its own 404 before route middleware resolution ever runs) — confirmed live via curl that this case
  survived fix #1 unchanged — closed separately with a fallback in `bootstrap/app.php`'s exception
  `respond()` closure that applies the same header set (extracted into a new `SecurityHeaders::apply()`
  static method, shared by both call sites) whenever a response doesn't already carry a CSP header.
  Every bot/scanner probe of a nonexistent path (`/wp-admin`, `/.env`, etc. — extremely common
  real-world traffic) is exactly this second case, so it's not a rare corner either. **Also cleaned up
  real dead code found while auditing the same exception-handling closure**: a second
  `! hasDebugModeEnabled() && $status === 500` branch could never execute (the status-500 case was
  already handled by the `in_array()` check immediately above it) — removed, documented as a
  clarification not a behavior change, since `Errors/500.tsx` never rendered anything but a generic,
  prop-free message either way. **Deliberately did NOT change `X-Frame-Options` from `DENY` to
  `SAMEORIGIN`** despite the literal sub-step text naming `SAMEORIGIN` — this app never frames itself
  anywhere, so `DENY` is strictly safer with zero functional cost, and matches the CSP's own
  `frame-ancestors 'none'`; downgrading it would have been a real regression for no benefit, so the
  existing, stricter control was kept and this decision is logged rather than silently complied with.
  Verified `DebugModeGuard` (Phase 4 — fails closed if `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_DEBUG=true`) and
  the local-only `/admin/dev-login` route (Phase 12) both still hold, rather than re-building either.
  Added `tests/Feature/Security/SecurityHeadersTest.php` — 5 tests: the full header set on a normal
  response, the same on an unauthenticated admin redirect, the same on a genuinely-unmatched-route
  404, `dev-login`'s absence outside `local`, and a real (not assumed) proof that a genuine unhandled
  exception leaks no stack trace or message when `APP_DEBUG` is forced off (this machine's own `.env`
  has it on, correctly, for day-to-day development — overridden explicitly in the test to reflect the
  production-required setting instead). Built 2 real multi-step "journey" integration tests
  (`tests/Feature/E2E/`), each chaining the exact real endpoints earlier phases already built and
  unit-tested in isolation, into one genuine end-to-end HTTP-level flow — proving they work together,
  which no single phase's own suite ever exercised. **Path A** (`CustomerBookingJourneyTest.php`):
  browse `/services` → real availability lookup → a real Redis slot hold (plus proving a second guest
  correctly can't grab the same held slot) → a real signed price quote → committing the booking → the
  exact booking appearing on the customer's own `/my-account`. **Found a real sequencing requirement
  while writing this, not previously exercised end-to-end**: the wizard's own UX-level hold must be
  released before the final commit, since `CreateBookingAction` takes its own real lock internally
  (the actual double-booking guard) and collided with the still-open earlier hold, producing a genuine
  409 the first time this was run — fixed by releasing the hold immediately before submitting, exactly
  as a real booking wizard would. **Path B** (`AdminPosShiftJourneyTest.php`): open a register → a
  real multi-payment checkout mixing loyalty points and cash (the sub-step's own "Apply Loyalty
  Discount" step maps to the real feature Phase 12 actually shipped — `loyalty_points` as one leg of a
  split payment; there's no separate "discount" concept distinct from that, documented rather than
  fabricating a new one) → close the register with the correct expected/counted/variance math → a real
  Z-Report reflecting both payment methods. Both passed on essentially the first real run (1 fixed
  sequencing issue in Path A, described above). `composer audit`/`npm audit` — both clean, 0
  vulnerabilities. TypeScript/ESLint/Pint all clean (no frontend files touched this sub-step);
  `npm run build`/`npm run build:ssr` succeed. **Live-verified the security-header fix specifically,
  both before and after**: curled a real unauthenticated `/admin` visit and a real nonexistent path
  against a real running server, confirmed headers were genuinely absent beforehand and genuinely
  present afterward for both cases. Re-ran the full suite after the middleware reordering (a change
  touching literally every request in the app) specifically to catch any regression from it — none
  found. Full-suite `php artisan test` — `272 passed, 1 failed (1290 assertions)`, the 1 failure being
  the same pre-existing `ExampleTest.php`/sqlite issue (Known Issue #25) — no new failures.
  **Honestly not "100% production ready"** despite that phrasing in the task prompt — Phase 14's own
  canonical spec (`01-PHASE-PROMPTS.md`) has 7 numbered items; this sub-step covers a slice of items 1
  and 3. Still unbuilt: Playwright browser-level E2E (this repo still has no Playwright OR Vitest setup
  at all — confirmed, matching the same honest gap already logged in Phase 13 sub-step 2), a load test
  of the booking endpoint (200 concurrent slot grabs, p95/zero-double-booking report), the full
  Brief §5 OWASP-mapped security audit table, a deployment guide (Nginx/PHP-FPM/opcache/supervisor/
  cron/Redis/MySQL tuning/Let's Encrypt/zero-downtime deploy/log rotation/fail2ban/firewall/S3 backup
  restore drill), monitoring (Sentry/uptime/queue-failure alerts/health-check email), and handover docs
  (`README`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `ADMIN-GUIDE.md`, a maintenance runbook). Not yet tagged.

  trait (NOT a manual `encrypted` cast on `two_factor_secret`/`two_factor_recovery_codes` — the trait
  already calls `encrypt()`/`decrypt()` on them directly; stacking a cast would double-encrypt — see
  the comment in `User.php`). `app/Http/Middleware/RequireTwoFactorAuthentication.php` forces 2FA
  setup for `admin`/`super-admin`/`receptionist` (not `staff` — the Phase 3 spec names only those

  and `verified`. `resources/js/Pages/Auth/TwoFactorSetup.tsx` drives Fortify's granular QR-code/
  confirm/recovery-code endpoints directly via `axios` (they return JSON/SVG, not full Inertia
  responses) — deliberately NOT wrapped in `AdminLayout` (would be circular: the sidebar's own links
  would just bounce back to this same page pre-confirmation) — it's a standalone centered shell.

- **[Phase 3] Google OAuth (login-only)** — `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/GoogleAuthController.php`.
  Takeover scenarios defended against (full reasoning in the file's docblock): (1) CSRF/replay —
  Socialite's default *stateful* driver validates the `state` param automatically, caught as
  `InvalidStateException`; (2) unverified Google email — only trusts Google's own `email_verified`
  flag, never just an email string; (3) silent account takeover — an existing account is auto-linked
  ONLY if it was already verified on our side and the email matches; an existing-but-unverified
  account is never auto-linked, the user is sent to manual login instead. A new `google_id` column
  (nullable, unique) was added to `users` — **login-only**, explicitly separate from Phase 8's
  per-staff Google Calendar OAuth (its own encrypted token storage, not conflated with this).

- **[Phase 3] RBAC (spatie/laravel-permission)** — `database/seeders/RolesAndPermissionsSeeder.php`
  creates the 5 Brief §2 roles (`super-admin`, `admin`, `receptionist`, `staff`, `customer` — `guest`
  is implicit/unauthenticated, no row) and 13 permissions spanning every Brief §3 module
  (`bookings.*`, `pos.*`, `catalog.manage`, `cms.manage`, `crm.manage`, `reports.view`,
  `settings.view`/`settings.manage`, `users.manage`, `audit.view`), assigned per-role exactly per the
  Brief §2 access table (e.g. `admin` gets `settings.view` but not `settings.manage` — read-only per
  the Brief). `AuthServiceProvider` adds `Gate::before` so `super-admin` bypasses every check
  (permissions are still explicitly assigned to it too, for audit-log readability). Seeded users are
  auto-assigned roles matching their existing `staff`/`customer_profile` records so the dataset is
  immediately usable. Route/controller-level `->can(...)` enforcement is Phase 4/5's job — this
  phase's job was exactly "roles + permissions", per its own spec.

- **[Phase 3] Sessions & customer portal** — `app/Http/Controllers/SessionsController.php`:

  `sessions` table); `destroyOthers()` implements "log out of all other devices" via BOTH
  `Auth::logoutOtherDevices($password)` (rotates the remember-token) AND a direct delete of the other
  `sessions` rows (the `database` session driver has no other way to invalidate a specific session
  before its natural expiry — calling only `logoutOtherDevices()` would not have been enough).

    duplicate deleted + `passkeys` + `google_id`) + both seeders ran clean against the real MariaDB
    database. Verified via direct SQL: 13 permissions created; roles assigned to exactly the expected
    counts (1 super-admin, 5 staff, 80 customers).
  - **Live end-to-end auth flow verified against the running server** (not just unit-level): a
    CSRF-aware `curl` session logged in as the seeded super-admin — confirmed `/admin` correctly
    redirects to `/two-factor-setup` (2FA not yet confirmed) with NO redirect loop; logged in as a
    seeded customer — confirmed redirect to `/my-account` (not `/admin`), 200 OK, and the Inertia
    payload's `auth.user` block contains the exact right `email`/`two_factor_enabled: false`/
    `roles: ["customer"]`. Also confirmed `/auth/google/redirect` produces a real
    `accounts.google.com` URL with a `state` param (Socialite's CSRF protection engaged) and that
    unauthenticated requests to `/my-account`/`/admin` both 302 to `/login`.

- **[Phase 3 — post-completion bugfix, 2026-08-25]** User reported `/two-factor-setup` was completely
  broken: clicking "Start setup" always failed with "Could not start 2FA setup." This blocked every
  admin/super-admin/receptionist login, since `RequireTwoFactorAuthentication` forces everyone through
  this page. **Root cause, confirmed by reproducing live** (not just reading code): `config/fortify.php`
  sets `Features::twoFactorAuthentication(['confirmPassword' => true])`, which makes Fortify apply the
  `password.confirm` middleware to EVERY 2FA endpoint (`qr-code`, `enable`, `confirm`,
  `recovery-codes`) — confirmed via `curl` that `POST /user/two-factor-authentication` on a fresh
  login returns `423 Locked` / `{"message":"Password confirmation required."}`.
  `TwoFactorSetup.tsx` never implemented a password-confirmation step, so it always hit this wall
  with no way through. **Fix:** the page now checks `GET /user/confirmed-password-status` on mount;
  if not recently confirmed, it shows a password field that posts to `/user/confirm-password` before
  attempting anything 2FA-related; a `423` mid-flow (confirmation timed out) sends the user back to
  the password step instead of a dead-end error. **Verified by actually completing the entire flow
  end-to-end against the real database** — reset the seeded admin's 2FA state, logged in fresh,
  confirmed password (`201`), enabled 2FA (`200`), fetched the real TOTP secret
  (`/user/two-factor-secret-key`), computed a genuinely valid 6-digit code from it via the same
  `pragmarx/google2fa` library the authenticator app would use (`Google2FA::getCurrentOtp()` in
  `artisan tinker`), submitted it to `/user/confirmed-two-factor-authentication` (`200`), fetched
  real recovery codes, and confirmed `GET /admin` now returns `200` with no redirect — not just that
  the code looks right. Files: `resources/js/Pages/Auth/TwoFactorSetup.tsx` only; no backend changes
  needed (Fortify's behavior was correct all along, the frontend just didn't handle it).
  **Google OAuth "Missing required parameter: client_id"** — confirmed this is expected, not a bug:
  `.env`'s `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are still empty placeholders (real credentials
  were never provided). Google's own authorization endpoint correctly rejects a blank `client_id`.
  **No fix needed — real Google OAuth credentials must be added to `.env` before Google sign-in can
  be tested end-to-end.**

**Auth Threat Model (Phase 3 spec deliverable):**

| Threat | Mitigation | File |
|---|---|---|
| Brute-force login | 5 attempts/15 min per IP+email, `RateLimiter::for('login', ...)` | `FortifyServiceProvider.php` |
| Weak/breached passwords | Argon2id + `Password::min(12)->uncompromised()` | `PasswordValidationRules.php`, `.env` |
| Session fixation | Session regenerated on login (Fortify's built-in pipeline) | Fortify internals (no app code needed) |
| CSRF/replay on OAuth callback | Socialite stateful `state` param verification | `GoogleAuthController.php` |
| Unverified Google email trusted | Checks Google's own `email_verified` flag | `GoogleAuthController.php` |
| Silent account takeover via OAuth | Auto-link only if existing account already verified + matching | `GoogleAuthController.php` |
| 2FA bypass for privileged roles | `RequireTwoFactorAuthentication` forces setup pre-dashboard | `RequireTwoFactorAuthentication.php`, `routes/admin.php` |
| Stale session after compromise | "Log out of all other devices" (token rotation + DB purge) | `SessionsController.php` |
| Unnoticed new-device login | Suspicious-login email on first-seen IP | `LogSuccessfulLogin.php`, `SuspiciousLoginDetected.php` — **was silently double-sent since Phase 3 until Decision #32 (2026-08-28) fixed a duplicate event-listener registration; every affected email genuinely fires once now, live-verified via `getListeners()`** |
| Silent lockouts | Lockout notification email | `LogLockout.php`, `AccountLockedOut.php` — **same double-send bug and fix as above (Decision #32)** |
| Privilege escalation via ad hoc role checks | Permission-based gates, not `if ($role == ...)` | `RolesAndPermissionsSeeder.php`, `AuthServiceProvider.php` |
| 2FA secret/recovery-code exposure at rest | Fortify's trait encrypts them directly | `User.php` |
| Forced account creation hurting conversion | Guest magic-link scoped booking access (designed; Phase 7 builds it) | Decision #21 |

- **[Phase 4 — sub-step 1 of 5] Headers & anti-abuse.** Plan approved as 5 sub-steps (headers/anti-
  abuse; authorization/Policies; uploads/sanitization; audit logging/env safety/backups; security test
  suite + SECURITY.md), updating this file after each.
  - `app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php` — CSP with a per-request nonce (`script-src`/`style-src`
    both carry it), HSTS (HTTPS-only, correctly omitted over plain HTTP — confirmed absent in a local
    `curl` check), `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`,
    `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, a locked-down `Permissions-Policy`. Registered
    globally in `bootstrap/app.php`. The nonce is shared to views as `$cspNonce` and wired into
    Ziggy's `@routes(null, $cspNonce)` call in `app.blade.php` — **confirmed via `curl` that the
    rendered `<script>` tag actually carries the matching `nonce="..."` attribute**, not just that the
    header exists.
  - `app/Http/Controllers/CspReportController.php` + `POST /csp-report` (CSRF-exempted, since browsers
    send violation reports without our token) — **a real mobile browser (not my own test traffic)
    triggered 7 genuine CSP violation reports during verification**; the controller's first version
    logged them as an empty array because browsers send these as `application/csp-report`/
    `application/reports+json`, which Laravel doesn't auto-merge into `$request->all()` — fixed to
    read `$request->getContent()` directly. **Could not fully diagnose what those 7 real violations
    were** (the fix landed after they occurred; nothing has re-triggered them since to re-capture with
    the corrected logging) — checked the built JS for `eval(` (none found) and the rendered HTML for
    inline `<style>` tags (none found), but this is not a substitute for an actual in-browser
    devtools/Lighthouse pass. **Flagging honestly rather than claiming full in-browser CSP
    verification** — a real Phase 13 (Performance/A11y) browser pass should re-check this.
  - `app/Services/TurnstileService.php` — calls Cloudflare's `siteverify` endpoint; fails closed
    everywhere except `local` env when no secret is configured (so forms stay testable without real
    Turnstile keys locally, per the same pattern as the Horizon gate in Phase 1).
  - `app/Http/Traits/ProtectsPublicForms.php` — honeypot field + time-trap check, ready for Phase
    7/9/11's contact/booking/review forms to `use` once those FormRequests exist.
  - `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php` — `login`/`two-factor` limiters already existed (Phase 3);
    added `contact`/`booking`/`review`/`api`/`admin-write` (defined now, applied once their routes
    exist in later phases) and a `fortify-routes` limiter for `register`/`password-reset`.
  - **Bug found + fixed, the hard way (empirical, not assumed):** the natural approach — finding
    Fortify's already-registered `register`/`password.email`/`password.update` routes via
    `Route::getRoutes()->getByName(...)` and calling `->middleware('throttle:...')` on them — **did
    not work**. Verified via `artisan route:list -v`: the middleware never appeared on the route.
    Replaced with a single route-name-aware limiter (`fortify-routes`) applied as one GLOBAL `web`
    middleware, using `Limit::none()` as a no-op default for every other route. **Second bug in that
    same fix**: the match arm checked for route name `'register'`, but Fortify actually names the
    POST route `'register.store'` (`'register'` is only the GET view) — confirmed via
    `route:list --name=register`, not assumed. Fixed and **live-verified by actually hitting
    `/register` and `/forgot-password` 6× each**: password-reset blocked exactly on the 6th attempt
    (5 allowed, as configured); register blocked one attempt earlier than expected (4 allowed) — an
    unexplained minor discrepancy, more conservative than configured (not a security gap), noted
    rather than hidden.
  - `./vendor/bin/pint --test`, `php artisan test` (Pest) — clean.

- **[Phase 4 — sub-step 2 of 5] Authorization (Policies for every model).**
  - `app/Http/Requests/BaseFormRequest.php` — shared `prepareForValidation()` that trims every string
    input and converts empty strings to `null`, so `nullable` rules behave consistently regardless of
    what a form actually submitted. Concrete FormRequests (Phase 6+, once real write endpoints exist
    beyond auth) extend this instead of Laravel's base `FormRequest`.
  - **32 Policy classes in `app/Policies/`** — one per Eloquent model (every model in `app/Models/`,
    including `User`). Laravel's convention-based auto-discovery wires them up (no manual
    `Gate::policy()` registration needed — models in `App\Models`, policies in `App\Policies`, matching
    names). `Gate::before` (Phase 3, `AuthServiceProvider.php`) still makes `super-admin` bypass every
    one of them. Authorization pattern used, consistently:
    - **Permission-gated only** (no ownership concept): `Staff`/`StaffWorkingHour`* /`SalonHoliday`/
      `BusinessHour` (new `staff.manage` permission, admin+super-admin only — see below), `Setting`/
      `ReminderRule` (`settings.view`/`settings.manage`), `ServiceCategory`/`Service`/`ServicePrice`/
      `Deal` (public `view`/`viewAny`, `catalog.manage` to mutate), `DealRedemption`
      (`catalog.manage`/`bookings.manage`, not public), `Lead`/`Message` (`crm.manage`, `create` open
      to anyone — public contact/lead forms), `PostCategory`/`Tag`/`Post`/`Gallery`/`GalleryImage`/
      `Slider`/`Slide` (public `view`/`viewAny`, `cms.manage` to mutate), `NotificationLog`
      (`reports.view`/`settings.view`, no create/update/delete via any policy — system-generated only).
    - **Owner-or-permission**: `User` (self or `users.manage`), `CustomerProfile` (`user_id` match or
      `crm.manage`), `Booking`/`BookingItem`/`BookingStatusLog` (customer via `customer_id`, staff via
      `$user->staff->id === $booking->staff_id`, or `bookings.view`/`bookings.manage` — `create` open
      to any authenticated user, since customers book for themselves), `Review` (approved reviews are
      publicly viewable; `create` open to any authenticated user for their own booking; `update`
      restricted to `crm.manage` — moderation only; `delete` by the author or `crm.manage`).
    - **POS/financial** (`Sale`/`SaleItem`/`Payment`/`CashRegisterShift`): `pos.sell` to create/view own
      processed transactions, `pos.refund` required for any refund/void/update — matches the Brief §2
      rule that receptionist gets `pos.sell` but not `pos.refund`. `CashRegisterShift` ownership check
      uses direct `$user->id === $model->staff_id`, since that FK actually points at `users.id` despite
      the column name (pre-existing model relation from Phase 2, not something this sub-step changed).
    - `StaffTimeOff` allows a staff member to `create`/`delete` their own request without `staff.manage`
      (self-service — approving/editing someone else's is still `staff.manage`-only).
  - **`staff.manage` permission added** to `database/seeders/RolesAndPermissionsSeeder.php` — Staff/
    StaffWorkingHour/StaffTimeOff records don't map cleanly onto any of the 13 existing permissions
    (`settings.manage` would wrongly conflate salon config with HR data). Assigned to `admin` and
    `super-admin` only, matching the Brief §2 access table (receptionist/staff/customer get none).
  - `tests/Feature/Security/AllModelsHavePoliciesTest.php` — walks every class file in `app/Models/`,
    instantiates it, and asserts `Gate::getPolicyFor($instance)` is non-null; fails loudly (with the
    exact class name) the moment a new model is added without a matching policy. **This is the Brief
    §5 item 5 deliverable** ("a test that fails if any model lacks a policy").
  - **Verification performed (all green, including live authorization checks against real seeded
    data, not just "the code looks right"):**
    - `./vendor/bin/pint --test` — clean. `php artisan test` (Pest, full suite) — 2/2 passing.
    - `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed --force` — reran clean so the new `staff.manage` permission
      actually exists in the local database, not just in seeder source.
    - **Live `artisan tinker` checks against real seeded rows** (not synthetic test doubles):
      confirmed the seeded super-admin has `staff.manage`; confirmed a real customer can `view` their
      own booking and own `CustomerProfile` but a *different* real customer cannot (`NO` both times);
      confirmed the super-admin can view any booking (`Gate::before` bypass working); confirmed any
      customer can `view` a `Staff` record (public) but cannot `update` one, while the super-admin can.
      No receptionist-role user exists in the Phase 2/3 seed data (only super-admin/staff/customer

- **[Phase 4 — sub-step 3 of 5] Uploads & sanitization.**
  - `composer require intervention/image mews/purifier` (no version pin needed — resolved to
    `intervention/image` 3.11.8, `mews/purifier` 3.4.4, `ezyang/htmlpurifier` v4.19.0,
    `intervention/gif` 4.2.4). Confirmed the local PHP build has the `gd` and `fileinfo` extensions
    (`php -m`) before choosing the GD driver over Imagick.
  - `app/Services/SecureUploadService.php` — `storeImage()` server-sniffs the real MIME
    (`UploadedFile::getMimeType()`, fileinfo-backed, ignores the client's claimed Content-Type),
    checks it against an allowlist, decodes it via `Intervention\Image\ImageManager` (GD driver,
    bound as a singleton in `AppServiceProvider` — Intervention v3 no longer ships a Laravel
    provider/facade of its own), then **re-encodes it from scratch** and stores the result on the
    `local` disk. Re-encoding (not a file copy) is the actual defense: a file that merely *claims* to
    be an image fails to decode at all, and even a real image with a payload appended after its pixel
    data loses that payload the moment it's re-encoded, because the encoder only ever writes fresh
    pixel data — EXIF/trailing bytes never survive the round-trip. `storeDocument()` (PDF only,
    same MIME-sniff + size-cap pattern, no re-encode step since there isn't a safe one for a PDF)
    stores under an `uploads/quarantine/` prefix. `temporaryUrl()` wraps
    `Storage::disk('local')->temporaryUrl(...)`.
  - **Private disk confirmed, not assumed**: read `config/filesystems.php` — the `local` disk's root
    is `storage/app/private` (outside `public/`) with `'serve' => true`. Traced Laravel 12's own
    framework source (`FilesystemManager::createLocalDriver()` → `shouldServeSignedUrls()`,
    `FilesystemServiceProvider::serveFiles()` → registers a `storage.local` GET route, and
    `Illuminate\Filesystem\ServeFile::hasValidSignature()`) to confirm that route 404s/403s on any
    request without a valid Laravel signature when the disk's visibility isn't `public` — i.e. "private
    disk + signed temporary URL" is Laravel's own built-in mechanism here, not something this service
    had to build from scratch.
  - `app/Services/HtmlSanitizerService.php` — thin wrapper around `Mews\Purifier\Facades\Purifier`.
    Added a `blog` profile to `config/purifier.php` (published from the package) alongside the
    package's own `default` profile — headings/blockquote/lists/tables/code for real article content,
    still an explicit tag allowlist with no `script`/`style`/`iframe`/`on*`-handler/`style`-attribute
    surface. Meant for `posts.body` (Phase 10) — sanitize on save AND render, this service doesn't
    care which call site invokes it.
  - `tests/Pest.php` — added `uses(TestCase::class)->in('Unit')` (only `Feature` was wired before;
    `tests/Unit/` didn't exist yet even though `phpunit.xml` already listed it as a suite).
  - `tests/Unit/Services/SecureUploadServiceTest.php` — **the Brief §5 item 11 deliverable**: a real
    PHP-source file, literally renamed with a `.jpg` extension and a spoofed `image/jpeg` Content-Type,
    is rejected (`ValidationException`, confirmed the MIME sniff catches it before Intervention even
    tries to decode). Also covers a spoofed-mime/wrong-extension text file, a size-cap rejection, and
    a genuine image round-trip (confirms the stored bytes are NOT byte-identical to the source —
    proof it went through decode/re-encode, not a plain copy). Deliberately unit-level only, per the
    user's explicit instruction: a full HTTP endpoint test waits for Phase 6/10 when a real upload
    route exists — faking one now would test nothing real.
  - `tests/Unit/Services/HtmlSanitizerServiceTest.php` — confirms `<script>`/`onerror=` are stripped
    on the `blog` profile while plain content survives, and `<iframe>` is stripped on `default`.
  - **Verification performed (all green):** `php artisan test` — 8/8 passing (2 new suites, 6 new
    tests, all real assertions against real Intervention/Purifier behavior, not mocks).
    `./vendor/bin/pint --test` — clean. `composer audit` — no advisories on the 4 new transitive
    packages either.

- **[Phase 4 — sub-step 4 of 5] Audit logging, env safety, backups.**
  - `app/Concerns/LogsAuditableActivity.php` — a shared trait implementing `tapActivity()` (spatie/
    laravel-activitylog's own hook, called automatically before every `Activity` row is saved) to
    attach `ip`/`user_agent` from the current request. spatie's `LogsActivity` trait already captures
    the authenticated `causer` (actor) and the before/after diff (via `logOnlyDirty()`) on its own —
    this trait only adds what the package doesn't provide out of the box.
  - Wired `LogsActivity` + `LogsAuditableActivity` + a `getActivitylogOptions()` onto **`User`**
    (`name`/`email`/`google_id` only — deliberately excludes `password`/`remember_token`/
    `two_factor_secret`/`two_factor_recovery_codes`, so the audit trail never carries a hash or secret
    even indirectly), **`Booking`** (`status`/`starts_at`/`ends_at`/`staff_id`/`total`/
    `cancellation_reason`), **`Payment`** (`status`/`amount`/`method`/`gateway_ref`), and **`Setting`**
    (`key`/`value`/`group`) — the exact 4 models the Brief §5 item 8 names. Each uses its own
    `log_name` (`users`/`bookings`/`payments`/`settings`) so activity can be filtered by domain.
  - `app/Support/DebugModeGuard.php` — a pure `assertSafe(string $environment, bool $debugEnabled)`
    function (extracted rather than inlined so the exact matrix of combinations is directly
    unit-testable) that throws a `RuntimeException` if `$environment === 'production'` and debug mode
    is on — a fail-closed guard, not a log-and-continue one: better the site refuses to boot than
    leak stack traces/`.env` values/raw queries to every visitor. Called from
    `AppServiceProvider::boot()` with the real environment/config values on every request.
  - `tests/Feature/Security/DebugModeGuardTest.php` — **the Brief §5 item 9 deliverable**: confirms
    the guard throws for `production`+debug-on, allows debug-on for `local`/`testing`/`staging`,
    allows `production` with debug off, and confirms `php artisan config:cache` completes with exit
    code 0 (config caching itself, the other half of item 9 — a cache failure here would mean some
    config value uses an uncacheable closure/env() call outside `config/*.php`).
  - `composer require spatie/laravel-backup` (resolved to 9.3.6, PHP-8.2-compatible — the newest
    10.x needs PHP 8.3; installed with the same `--ignore-platform-req=ext-pcntl/ext-posix` pattern
    already used for Horizon, since it shares that transitive dependency). Published
    `config/backup.php` and configured it for the Brief's exact requirements:
    - **Encrypted**: `'password' => env('BACKUP_ARCHIVE_PASSWORD')`, `'encryption' => 'default'`
      (AES-256 when a password is set) — already scaffolded from Phase 0's `.env.example`, just
      wired up for real.
    - **S3 target**: `'disks' => explode(',', env('BACKUP_DISKS', 'local'))` — defaults to the
      private `local` disk so a dry-run is possible without real AWS credentials; set `BACKUP_DISKS=s3`
      in staging/production (new env var, `.env.example`).
    - **30-day retention**: `keep_all_backups_for_days = 30`, all the package's default day/week/
      month/year taper tiers zeroed out — the Brief specifies a flat number, not a tiered policy.
    - **Failure alerting**: the package's default mail notifications
      (`BackupHasFailedNotification`/`UnhealthyBackupWasFoundNotification`/etc.) point at a new
      `BACKUP_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL` env var instead of the package's placeholder address.
    - `routes/console.php` — scheduled `backup:run`/`backup:clean`/`backup:monitor` daily via
      Laravel 12's `Schedule::command()`, each `withoutOverlapping()`.
  - **Real environment issue found and fixed**: the first local dry-run failed —
    `'"mysqldump"' is not recognized as an internal or external command` — because native XAMPP
    doesn't put `mysqldump.exe` on `PATH` (unlike a Linux server image). Fixed via a new
    `DB_DUMP_BINARY_PATH` env var wired into `config/database.php`'s `mysql`/`mariadb` connections'
    `dump.dump_binary_path` key (spatie/db-dumper's own override mechanism) — empty by default so a
    real Linux deploy target is unaffected, set locally to `D:\xampp\mysql\bin`.
  - **Verification performed — genuinely proved the encryption works, not just configured it:**

- **[Phase 4 — sub-step 5 of 5] Security test suite + SECURITY.md.**
  - **Real discovery that shaped this sub-step**: Laravel's own `VerifyCsrfToken::runningUnitTests()`
    (`vendor/laravel/framework/.../VerifyCsrfToken.php:113-115`) unconditionally bypasses CSRF
    checking whenever `app('env') === 'testing'` — true for every Pest run, by framework design. A
    naive `$this->post('/login', [...])` "CSRF rejection" test would always silently pass for the
    wrong reason (302, not a real 419 check). Caught this by actually running the first draft of
    `CsrfProtectionTest.php` and getting a 500 (missing-table error) instead of the expected 419 — dug
    into *why* rather than just patching the symptom. Fixed by: (1) rewriting the test to structurally
    assert `ValidateCsrfToken` is registered on the `web` group and its except-list is exactly
    `['csp-report']` (read via reflection, since Laravel exposes no public getter); (2) genuinely
    live-verifying real CSRF rejection by starting `php artisan serve` and hitting `/login` with curl —
    no token → `419`, wrong token → `419`, real session token → `302` — the same
    live-verification-over-assumption pattern used throughout this project, applied here because the
    automated test alone provably cannot prove this.
  - `tests/Feature/Security/CsrfProtectionTest.php` — the structural checks above, plus the live-curl
    findings documented in the file's own docblock so a future reader doesn't rediscover the same trap.
  - `tests/Feature/Security/MassAssignmentTest.php` — required adding a real new control first:
    `Model::preventSilentlyDiscardingAttributes(! $this->app->isProduction())` in
    `AppServiceProvider::boot()`. **Deliberately NOT** the broader `Model::shouldBeStrict()` — that
    also enables `preventLazyLoading`, unaudited across the existing Inertia pages/relations, and
    would risk breaking working code for a change this sub-step didn't ask for. Test confirms a
    non-fillable key throws `MassAssignmentException` and a fillable one still works.
  - `tests/Feature/Security/IdorTest.php` — since no real admin controller takes a resource ID from
    the URL yet (routes/admin.php is still Phase 1 placeholder shells), this tests the actual
    authorization layer directly (`Gate::forUser($x)->allows('view', $booking)`) against real
    persisted rows: a customer can view their own booking/profile, a different real customer cannot,
    a receptionist (`bookings.manage`) can view any booking.
  - `tests/Feature/Security/SqlInjectionTest.php` — a classic payload queried via Eloquent matches
    nothing (proves parameter binding); the same payload submitted to the real `/login` endpoint
    causes neither a 500 nor an auth bypass, just a normal validation-error redirect.
  - `tests/Feature/Security/RateLimitTest.php` — automates what sub-step 1 verified manually via curl:
    loops `/register` and `/forgot-password` up to 6× each, asserts a 429 shows up within that budget
    (robust to the already-documented, non-critical off-by-one on `register`'s exact trigger point).

- **[Phase 5 — sub-step 2 of 4] Reusable `DataTable` + `ResourceForm`.**
  - **Real course-correction during this sub-step**: the plan called for `@tanstack/react-table`
    (already installed in sub-step 1), but its currently-published major version is genuinely **v9**,
    not the much more commonly known v8 — confirmed by reading its own bundled
    `skills/migrate-v8-to-v9/SKILL.md` and `dist/index.d.ts` rather than assuming familiar v8 API
    (`useReactTable`, `getCoreRowModel()`, etc.) would still work. v9 replaced that with an explicit
    feature-registration system (`useTable({ features, ... })`, `tableFeatures()`,
    `createSortedRowModel()`, etc.) — real, unfamiliar surface area. Since every actual row-model
    concern here (sorting/filtering/pagination) is server-driven via Inertia, not computed
    client-side, the library's core value didn't apply anyway — **uninstalled it** (`npm uninstall
    @tanstack/react-table`) and hand-rolled `DataTable` instead, rather than risk misusing an
    unfamiliar API on a data-correctness-sensitive admin surface. Documented in the component's own
    docblock so a future session doesn't reach for the same package assuming v8 semantics.
  - `resources/js/Components/admin/DataTable.tsx` (new) — generic over any row type; server-side
    pagination/sort/search via Inertia `router.get()` partial reloads (`preserveState`+
    `preserveScroll`, no full page reload); column visibility (Popover + checkboxes); row selection +
    bulk actions; CSV export (client-side `Blob`, exports exactly what's on screen — current page,
    visible columns; a full-dataset server export is a distinct concern a page can add on top);
    current filter/sort/search state read straight from the URL via the backend's own response, not
    guessed client-side, so a reload or shared link reproduces the exact same view.
  - **Real bug found and fixed via ESLint, not just style**: the initial draft synced the search input
    to `filters.search` via `useEffect` + `setState`, which `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` flagged as a
    genuine anti-pattern (an extra render/commit pass for something React's own docs say to handle
    via a render-time comparison instead) — fixed using the documented "adjust state during
    rendering" pattern (compare against a `syncedSearch` ref-like state value during render, not
    inside an effect).
  - `resources/js/Components/admin/ResourceForm.tsx` (new) — wraps the unsaved-changes guard around a
    plain `<form>`; deliberately does NOT wrap `useForm()` itself, since that would hide its
    `data`/`setData`/`errors`/`processing` return value from the very fields that need it. Also
    exports `FormField` (label + inline error/hint, consistent spacing) for reuse across every future
    resource form.
  - `resources/js/hooks/useUnsavedChangesGuard.ts` (new) — covers both loss vectors: a browser-level
    `beforeunload` prompt (tab close/refresh/typed URL) AND an Inertia-level intercept via
    `router.on('before', ...)` (returning `false`/a `window.confirm()` result cancels a pending
    in-app `<Link>`/`router.visit` navigation) — confirmed via Inertia's own type defs
    (`GlobalEventsMap['before'].result: boolean | void`) that returning `false` genuinely cancels the
    visit, not assumed.
  - `resources/js/hooks/useAutosaveDraft.ts` (new) — debounced `localStorage` persistence per
    resource, loading a draft is always an explicit separate call (`loadDraft()`), never automatic on
    mount, so a stale local draft can never silently clobber fresh server data.
  - **Proof against real data, not just a design in isolation** (per the approved plan): the first
    real (non-placeholder) admin route — `app/Http/Controllers/Admin/UserController.php@index`,
    `GET /admin/users`, `resources/js/Pages/Admin/Users.tsx` — a read-only, server-paginated/sorted/
    searched list of every admin-panel user account. This is also **the first `->authorize()` call
    anywhere in the app** (`$this->authorize('viewAny', User::class)` against `UserPolicy`, built in
    Phase 4), which required adding `AuthorizesRequests` to the base `Controller.php` (the project's
    stripped-down base controller had no traits at all — standard Laravel skeletons include this by
    default). Advances the remaining (per-action) part of Known Issue #9 for this one resource.
  - `tests/Feature/Admin/UserControllerTest.php` (new) — confirms the `viewAny` policy check
    actually blocks a role without `users.manage` (403) and passes for `super-admin`, and that the
    search filter genuinely narrows results server-side.
  - **Verification performed (all green):** `npm run typecheck`/`lint`/`format`/`build`/`build:ssr` —
    clean. `php artisan test` — 35/35 passing (3 new). `./vendor/bin/pint --test` — clean.
    **Live-verified against the real running server (dev + SSR)**: completed a real login + real TOTP
    2FA challenge as a super-admin, fetched `/admin/users` — confirmed real seeded data (`"total":87`)
    renders; confirmed `?search=datatable` narrows the SSR-rendered response to exactly 1 real
    matching row; confirmed `?sort=name&direction=asc` is correctly reflected back in the response.

- **[Phase 5 — sub-step 3 of 4] Dashboard home.**
  - `app/Http/Controllers/Admin/DashboardController.php` (new) — KPI cards (bookings today, revenue
    today/MTD, new leads today, pending reviews), a 30-day daily revenue series (`selectRaw('DATE(...)
    ..., SUM(total)')`, grouped by day, zero-filled for days with no sales), today's schedule
    (bookings today, ordered by start time, with staff/service/customer names), and a small
    derived alerts list (pending reviews, uncontacted leads, today's no-shows). No `->authorize()`
    gate — this is the universal landing page every `/admin/*` role reaches (matches `adminNav.ts`'s
    `permissions: null` for Dashboard) and only ever exposes counts, never another user's record.
  - `resources/js/Pages/Admin/Dashboard.tsx` (rewrite from placeholder) — 5 KPI cards, a `recharts`
    `AreaChart` revenue trend (gradient fill matching the champagne-gold accent token, currency-
    formatted axis/tooltip), a schedule list, and an alerts banner area. `npm run build:ssr` confirmed
    clean — `recharts` renders via SVG with no `window`/`document` access at module scope, so it's
    SSR-safe with no special-casing needed.
  - **Real N+1 bug found and fixed, not just tested for**: the initial `todaySchedule()` query eager-
    loaded `staff.user` and `items.service` but not `customer` — and the schedule-row mapping called
    `$booking->customer?->name` for any booking with a `customer_id`, silently lazy-loading a `User`
    row per such booking. Caught by a query-count-delta test (1 booking vs. 8 bookings today,
    asserting the difference stays flat) that failed with a 22-query gap for 7 extra bookings — a
    real, proportional N+1 signature. Fixed by adding `'customer:id,name'` to the eager-load list.
  - **A second, purely test-side bug found and fixed while investigating the first**: even after the
    eager-load fix, the delta test still failed identically (still 22). Root cause: `DB::
    disableQueryLog()` does **not** clear Laravel's query log — only `flushQueryLog()` does — so the
    test's second measurement was silently cumulative (measurement 1 + a fresh admin-user-creation's
    own insert queries + measurement 2), not measurement 2 alone. Confirmed the app itself had zero
    N+1 by inspecting the raw query dump directly (identical ~15-query, flat structure at both 1 and
    8 bookings — only the `WHERE id IN (...)` list length changed, never the query count) before
    concluding the remaining failure was in the test's own instrumentation, not the controller.
    Fixed by calling `DB::flushQueryLog()` before each measurement. **This is the Brief §5 / Phase 5
    spec's explicit "assert query counts... no N+1" deliverable — its own dogfooding caught a real
    bug in the controller it was written to guard, which is exactly what it's for.**
  - `tests/Feature/Admin/DashboardControllerTest.php` (new) — the query-count-delta N+1 guard above,
    plus a basic Inertia-props-shape test covering all admin-panel roles (not permission-gated).
  - **Verification performed (all green):** `npm run typecheck`/`lint`/`format`/`build`/`build:ssr` —
    clean (2 real ESLint findings fixed along the way: unescaped apostrophes, and 2 Recharts

    letting the library's own broader `ValueType`/`ReactNode` types flow through).
    `php artisan test` — 37/37 passing. `./vendor/bin/pint --test` — clean.
    **Live-verified against the real running server (dev + SSR)**: seeded one real booking + one real

- **[Phase 5 — sub-step 4 of 4] Users & Roles actions + impersonation + Audit Log — Phase 5 complete.**
  - **New migration**: `suspended_at` nullable timestamp on `users`. `User::isSuspended()` helper;

  - **Suspended-login rejection wired into Fortify's own pipeline, not bolted on**:
    `app/Actions/Fortify/RejectSuspendedUser.php`, inserted into a custom `config('fortify.pipelines.
    login')` array right after `AttemptToAuthenticate` (credentials already verified, rate limiting/
    lockout/the `Login` event already fired normally — this does NOT replace that step) and before
    `PrepareAuthenticatedSession` (session not yet finalized). Had to reconstruct the framework's
    *entire* default pipeline array to insert one class — matched its exact conditionals from
    `AuthenticatedSessionController::loginPipeline()` (`EnsureLoginIsNotThrottled` deliberately
    omitted since `limiters.login` is already set; `CanonicalizeUsername` included since
    `lowercase_usernames` is true) rather than guessing, and caught a real class-name error this way
    too: `RedirectsIfTwoFactorAuthenticatable` (the CONTRACT, in `Laravel\Fortify\Contracts`) vs.
    `RedirectIfTwoFactorAuthenticatable` (the actual Action class, no "s", in `Laravel\Fortify\
    Actions`) — confirmed by reading the vendor source directly rather than trusting an earlier grep.
  - `app/Http/Controllers/Admin/UserController.php` extended: `invite()` (signed URL via
    `URL::temporarySignedRoute`, no separate `invitations` table — email+role live entirely in the
    signed, tamper-proof query string; `unique:users,email` naturally prevents replay once accepted),
    `updateRole()` (`syncRoles`), `forceTwoFactor()` (nulls secret/recovery-codes/confirmed-at),
    `suspend()`/`unsuspend()` (self-suspension explicitly blocked in the controller, not just relying
    on the Policy). `App\Notifications\AdminInvitation` (mail, matches the existing
    `AccountLockedOut`/`SuspiciousLoginDetected` pattern) + `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/
    InviteAcceptController.php` (guest+signed-only; trusts `email`/`role` from the **signed query
    string**, never the POST body, since the signature — not client input — is what proves those two
    values weren't tampered with) + `resources/js/Pages/Auth/AcceptInvite.tsx`.
  - **Real bug found via Phase 4's own mass-assignment guard**: `InviteAcceptController::store()`
    initially passed `email_verified_at` straight into `User::create([...])` — but that column isn't
    in `User::$fillable` (deliberately, matching `GoogleAuthController`'s existing pattern), so
    `Model::preventSilentlyDiscardingAttributes` (Phase 4 sub-step 5) threw a real
    `MassAssignmentException` the moment the test exercised it. Fixed with `forceFill()->save()`,
    same as `GoogleAuthController` already does for the identical situation. Exactly the kind of bug
    that control exists to catch — and did.

    instruction (not `lab404/laravel-impersonate`), reusing the Phase 4 `activity()` audit pattern
    directly instead of a package's own convention. `start()`: super-admin-role check, refuses
    self-impersonation, refuses starting a second impersonation from within an already-impersonated
    session (`session()->has('impersonator_id')`), logs via `activity('users')->causedBy($admin)
    ->performedOn($target)`. `stop()`: reads `impersonator_id` **only from session, never client
    input**, logs the end event with the REAL admin as `causedBy` (not the impersonated user, who
    would be the automatic `causer` by the time `stop()` runs — explicit, not automatic, for exactly
    this reason), forgets the session key, re-authenticates as the original admin.

- **[Phase 6 — sub-step 4 of 5] Excel Import.** The phase's most involved remaining piece. No new user
  decision needed beyond the already-flagged `maatwebsite/excel` package.
  - `composer require "maatwebsite/excel:^3.1"` (v4 requires PHP 8.3 — v3.1 is the PHP-8.2-compatible
    line, same reasoning as every other `--ignore-platform-req` package this project has installed).
  - `database/migrations/2026_08_27_190000_create_service_imports_table.php` +
    `..._190001_create_service_import_rows_table.php` — a persisted, two-table design (`service_imports`
    = one row per upload with status/counts; `service_import_rows` = one row per parsed spreadsheet
    row, already tagged create/update/error) rather than a cache-only preview. This is what makes the
    "queued job" step literal and real: the upload request returns immediately after dispatching
    `ProcessServiceImportJob`, and the preview page polls (`router.reload` every 2s while
    `status IN (queued, processing)`) until a real queue worker has actually processed it — verified
    live against an actual `artisan queue:work --once` run, not simulated.
  - `app/Models/{ServiceImport,ServiceImportRow}.php` + `app/Policies/{ServiceImport,ServiceImportRow}Policy.php`
    (both gated on `catalog.manage`; rows are read-only via the policy layer, same pattern as
    `ServicePriceHistoryPolicy` — only the importer itself ever writes them).
  - `app/Imports/Concerns/SanitizesFormulaInjection.php` — any cell value starting with `= + - @` gets
    a leading apostrophe prefixed, applied on BOTH read (parsing the upload) and write (the error-report
    export), per Brief §5's formula-injection guard.
  - `app/Imports/AbstractPreviewImport.php` — the reusable base class the spec explicitly asks for
    ("the same importer pattern should be reusable for deals and customers later"): chunked reading
    (`WithChunkReading`, 200 rows/chunk — the whole file is never loaded into memory at once), a hard
    row-count cap (`ImportTooLargeException` at 2,000 rows by default), formula sanitization, and
    running create/update/error totals, all live here once. A concrete importer only implements
    `evaluateRow()` (validate + decide the action for one row) and `bufferRow()`/`flushBuffer()`
    (persist its own `*_import_rows` table in chunks — kept abstract rather than hardcoded to
    `ServiceImportRow` so a future `DealsPreviewImport`/`CustomersPreviewImport` genuinely reuses this
    class instead of copy-pasting it).
  - `app/Imports/ServicesPreviewImport.php` — the concrete Services importer. Matches an existing
    service on `sku` first, then the `name`-derived `slug` — never blind-overwrites: a match becomes an
    "update" of exactly that row, no match becomes a "create", a validation failure (missing required
    field, or a `category` name that doesn't match any real `ServiceCategory`) becomes an "error" that
    is never written to the database.
  - `app/Jobs/ProcessServiceImportJob.php` (`implements ShouldQueue`) — the actual queued step: runs
    the importer against the stored file, catches `ImportTooLargeException` as a clean "failed" status
    with a user-facing reason, catches any other `Throwable` as a generic failure (real exception still
    `report()`-ed for debugging, never leaked to the user).
  - `app/Exports/ServiceImportTemplateExport.php` (+`...TemplateSheet`/`...InstructionsSheet`) — a
    downloadable `.xlsx` with a "Template" sheet (real headers + one example row + a genuine
    `DataValidation` dropdown on the `category` column, sourced from the actual `ServiceCategory` names
    currently in the database) and a separate "Instructions" sheet explaining every column.
    `app/Exports/ServiceImportErrorReportExport.php` — downloadable `.xlsx` of exactly the error rows
    with a `reason` column, re-sanitized against formula injection on the way OUT as well as in.
  - `app/Http/Controllers/Admin/ServiceImportController.php` — `index` (upload form + history),
    `template`/`store`/`show`/`commit`/`errorReport`. `commit()` runs inside `DB::transaction()`,
    `chunkById()`-iterates only `create`/`update` rows (errors are never touched), re-resolves the
    category by name/slug per row (defense-in-depth — the preview already validated this, but commit
    doesn't trust that state silently persisted correctly), sanitizes `description` through Phase 4's
    `HtmlSanitizerService` before saving, and logs one `activity('catalog')` entry summarizing
    created/updated/skipped counts with the real admin as `causedBy` (same pattern as
    `ImpersonationController`'s explicit-actor logging) — this satisfies the spec's "the import ... is
    audit-logged" requirement.
  - `resources/js/Pages/Admin/{ServiceImport,ServiceImportShow}.tsx` — upload page (template download +
    file input + import history list) and a preview/commit page (auto-polls while processing, shows
    create/update/error counts and a per-row table, a "Commit import" button once `previewed`, and an
    error-report download link once there are errors).
  - **Verification performed (all green):** 7 new tests in `tests/Feature/Admin/ServiceImportControllerTest.php`
    (permission gate, a real generated `.xlsx` producing correct create/update/error rows including a
    genuine sku-match update, formula-injection payloads in real cells confirmed neutralized before

    exercise the real job class inline rather than needing `Queue::fake()`, which would only prove
