  (`public/images/looks smart beauty Salon in Lahore.mp4`, ~536 KB, already on disk) behind a
  two-layer scrim — a warm champagne radial wash for brand tone plus a dark vertical gradient that
  guarantees text contrast whatever frame is underneath. Path built with `encodeURI()` rather than a
  hand-typed `%20` string, so the real filename stays readable at the call site; verified the server
  serves it at the encoded path (`200`, `video/mp4`). **No CSP change was needed and this was checked
  rather than assumed**: there is no `media-src` directive, so it falls back to `default-src 'self'`,
  and the video is same-origin. Copy/CTAs set per spec: h1 "Looks Smart Beauty Salon", the "modern
  sanctuary…in Lahore" sub-description, and "Book Appointment"/"View Services".
  **The fallback chain is real, not decorative.** The poster renders server-side and the `<video>`
  mounts only on the client, which solves three separate problems: `prefers-reduced-motion` cannot be
  known during SSR; React does not serialise `muted` into server HTML (it applies it as a DOM
  property on hydration) so a server-rendered `<video autoplay>` gets autoplay *blocked* by Chrome;
  and `play()` rejects outright under data/battery saver, which must be caught or it becomes an
  unhandled rejection. Poster-first also keeps the video off the critical path.
  **A real trap found and worked around, caught by a browser test rather than reasoning:**
  `useReducedMotion()` from framer-motion 13 is `useState(prefersReducedMotion.current)` — a
  **one-shot** read whose own source comments concede it never updates. Under SSR that module ref is
  `null`, so the hook locks in a falsy value that never corrects after hydration, and it kept serving
  the looping video to reduced-motion users. Replaced with a direct
  `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` listener. **That hook is fine for animation config
  and wrong for branching what gets rendered** — worth remembering, since `PublicLayout` uses it too
  (harmlessly, for transition config).
  **(2) "Our Specialized Services" section.** Replaced the old "The menu / A little luxury, made
  practical." block: new centred header and subhead, category filter pills, a responsive grid
  (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4` — 4/2/1 per spec, asserted by measuring real computed
  `gridTemplateColumns` at 1440px and 390px), cards carrying image/name/duration/PKR price with
  "+ Book" → `/book?service={id}` and "Details" → `/services/{slug}`, accent-coloured active pills
  and primary buttons, and a centred "View All Services →" CTA to `/services`.
  **The pills are driven by the real categories from the database, deliberately not the list in the
  task.** The spec said "use current site service categories" and then listed `HAIR | MAKEUP & BRIDAL
  | NAILS & SPA | WAXING & BODY | THREADING & BROWS` — which is the **superseded** set from ad hoc
  task 6, replaced by task 7's own catalog overhaul at the user's instruction. The live categories are
  Hair Styling & Treatments / Skin & Facial Care / Bridal & Party Makeup / Eyelashes, Waxing &
  Threading / Massage, Spa & Special Services (there is no longer a Nails & Spa or Threading & Brows
  category — nails is a single service inside Massage/Spa/Specials). Honoured the stated intent over
  the stale literal list, and rendering from `categories` means the pills cannot drift again.
  `home()` also had to change: it fetched only 6 featured services, which left most pills showing an
  empty grid — now grouped by category with 8 each (featured first), so every pill has cards. The
  `categories` prop it had been passing since Phase 9 was previously unused by the page.
  **(3) A real content bug fixed, outside the spec but factually wrong on the live homepage.** The
  bottom info band hardcoded `123 Beauty Lane / Your neighborhood, beautifully.` and
  `Monday–Saturday 9:00 am–7:00 pm` — placeholder text that survived ad hoc task 6 because that task
  only reworked the footer, and which contradicted both the real address and the salon's actual
  seven-day 10:00-21:00 hours. Now reads from the shared `site` prop, so it cannot drift from
  Settings again.
  **Verification:** new `tests/e2e/home-hero.spec.ts` — 7 real-browser Chromium tests, all passing.
  These assert **actual playback state, not markup**: `readyState >= 2`, `paused === false`, and
  `currentTime` genuinely advancing, plus `muted`/`loop` as DOM properties and the percent-encoded
  `src`. Also covered: hero copy and both CTAs, pill filtering (a skin service present and a hair
  service absent after clicking "Skin & Facial Care"), Book/Details/View-All hrefs, the 4-col/1-col
  measurement, the reduced-motion branch (zero `<video>` elements, poster still filling the hero),

| 21 | 2026-08-25 | **Guest bookings get passwordless "magic-link" access instead of forced account creation.** Guest booking stays the default (protects conversion); a signed, booking-scoped link (emailed on confirmation) lets a guest view/reschedule/cancel *that one booking* with no password and no session. Full accounts remain optional, for people who want history/reviews. Design only this phase — **implementation is Phase 7's job** (the booking engine doesn't exist yet). Design: <br>• `URL::temporarySignedRoute()`, keyed on the booking's `code` (not the sequential `id`) to avoid leaking enumerable IDs in the emailed link. <br>• **Expiry = `booking.starts_at` + 24h grace period**, capped at a defensive ceiling (90 days) in case `starts_at` is far out — not a fixed short wall-clock window. This is deliberately "short" *relative to the booking's own lifecycle* (dies shortly after the appointment happens or would have happened) rather than an arbitrary few-minutes window that would make the link useless for a booking made weeks out (`max_advance_days` is seeded at 60). <br>• **Runtime status check layered on top of the signature**: even a still-cryptographically-valid link gets a `410 Gone` the moment `booking.status` becomes `cancelled`/`completed`/`no_show` — signed URLs alone don't know about mutable app state, so this check is what actually satisfies "invalidated once cancelled or completed." <br>• **Rate limited** (throttle middleware, e.g. 10/min/IP) — defense in depth on top of the HMAC signature already making guessing infeasible. <br>• **Single-purpose by construction, not by a special exclusion rule**: the flow never calls `Auth::login()` or issues a session/token — it's a scoped capability URL for one resource, not an authentication mechanism. That's what stops "replay to escalate": there is no account session to pivot from, and every mutating action (reschedule/cancel) re-validates the same signature on every request rather than trusting one initial check. <br>• **Reviews still require a full verified account** (Brief §5) — a magic-link visit never authenticates `Auth::user()`, so ordinary `auth`+`verified` middleware on the review-posting route already blocks it; no special-casing needed. | Forcing account creation for every booking (rejected — kills conversion, and the user was explicit about this); a long-lived flat token with no status check (rejected — would stay "valid" after cancellation); reusing the same link as a general login mechanism (rejected — turns a single-resource capability into an account-takeover surface) |

**⚠ If a future session is asked to add deposits or prepaid packages:** re-read Decisions #19/#20
first. Both would touch `bookings` (new columns or a new related table), `services` (a package needs
to reference which services it bundles), and the Phase 7 booking flow (deposit collection at
checkout, package-redemption instead of payment). Neither is a bug to "fix" — they were scoped out on
purpose.

**Hard gate tied to Decision #10:** Redis MUST be installed and wired (real driver switch back to
`redis` for session/cache/queue, plus the atomic slot-lock logic in Brief §4) before Phase 7 (Booking
Engine) begins — double-booking prevention depends on it. Tracked as blocking tech debt in §10 #6.

  `2026_09_26_091837_add_deal_id_to_sale_items_table` — new nullable `sale_items.deal_id` (FK,

  MariaDB database.

  cart-level Discount %/Tax % override fields persist the exact percentage typed, not just the
  resulting dollar amount — needed so a resumed held sale restores the real percentage and the
  receipt/invoice can print "Discount (12%)"/"Tax (5%)". Applied via `php artisan migrate` against the
  real local MariaDB database.

- **Migrations run through:** `2026_08_31_000104_add_notification_preferences_to_customer_profiles_table` — 54 migrations total. `customer_profiles` now stores `marketing_opt_in`, `email_opt_out`, `sms_opt_out`, `whatsapp_opt_out`, and nullable `consented_at`; `notification_logs.reminder_key` remains the unique idempotency key from migration `2026_08_31_000103`.
- **Migrations run through:** `2026_08_28_080815_create_notifications_table` — 52 migrations total
  (Phase 8 sub-step 1 added the standard Laravel `notifications` table for the `database` notification
  channel), applied cleanly via `php artisan migrate --force`.
- **Migrations run through (Phase 7):** `2026_08_28_000000_make_bookings_unique_index_status_aware` — 51
  migrations total, applied cleanly via `php artisan migrate --force` (incremental, not a fresh
  reseed).
- **Phase 7 sub-step 3 schema changes:** `bookings.active_slot_key` (MySQL/MariaDB — a generated
  column, NULL for cancelled/no_show/soft-deleted rows) + `bookings_active_slot_unique` index
  replacing the old plain `UNIQUE(staff_id, starts_at)`; a plain `bookings_staff_id_index` added
  alongside (required before the old unique index could be dropped — MariaDB won't drop the only
  index supporting a foreign key). SQLite (tests) gets an equivalent partial unique index instead.
- **Migrations run through (Phase 6):** `2026_08_27_190001_create_service_import_rows_table` — 44 from
  Phase 2 + medialibrary's `media` table + the sku/image_path migration + the price history table +
  the deal/category pivot + the two import tables.
- **Phase 6 sub-step 3 schema changes:** `deal_service_category` pivot table (`deal_id`,
  `service_category_id`, composite PK) — deals can now target categories in addition to individual
  services (`deal_service`, already existed from Phase 2).
- **Phase 6 sub-step 4 schema changes:** `service_imports` (one row per upload — status/counts/who) and
  `service_import_rows` (one row per parsed spreadsheet row, tagged create/update/error, with the
  sanitized parsed data and any validation errors as JSON).
- **Phase 6 sub-step 1 schema changes:** `media` table (spatie/laravel-medialibrary, polymorphic —
  `model_type`/`model_id`, `collection_name`, `file_name`, `mime_type`, `conversions_disk`, etc.).
  `services.sku` added (nullable, unique). `service_categories.image_path` dropped (superseded by the
  `media` table; confirmed unused in any factory/seeder first).
- **Phase 6 sub-step 2 schema changes:** `service_price_history` table (append-only — `const
  UPDATED_AT = null`; `service_id`, nullable `service_price_id` FK, `price_list`, nullable
  `old_price`/`new_price`, `changed_by` FK to `users`, `reason`).
- **Tables created (44 original + 2 new = 46 total):**
  - *Framework/Phase 1:* `users` (+ 2FA columns + soft deletes added in Phase 2), `password_reset_tokens`,
    `sessions`, `cache`, `cache_locks`, `jobs`, `job_batches`, `failed_jobs`
  - *Identity/RBAC (spatie, published not hand-written):* `roles`, `permissions`, `model_has_roles`,

| **Phase 13 specific — CSP stays locked down unless analytics is actually configured, and never fails to generate** | ✅ | `app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php::buildCsp()` — `'strict-dynamic'` + the real Google domains are only added to `script-src`/`frame-src`/`img-src`/`connect-src` when `integrations.google_tag_manager_id`/`google_analytics_id` are actually set; the `Setting::get()` reads are wrapped in `try/catch`, failing safe to the strict policy (a header needed on every response can never be allowed to throw) | **Live-verified with a real single-request nonce comparison**: curled the homepage with GTM/GA4 configured and confirmed the CSP header's nonce and the rendered `<script nonce="...">` tags' nonce were the exact same value, then cleared the settings and confirmed the header/tags both reverted. `tests/Feature/PerformanceAndA11yTest.php` (4 tests) + `tests/Feature/Security/XssPayloadTest.php` (the fail-safe fix's own regression test) |
| **Phase 14 specific — security headers genuinely present on every response, including error pages** | ✅ (fixed this sub-step — was a real, previously-undetected gap) | `app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php` — `prepend`ed to the `web` group (not `append`ed) and now catches exceptions thrown by any route-level middleware, rendering + header-applying the resulting response itself; `bootstrap/app.php`'s exception `respond()` closure applies the same header set as a fallback for paths matching no route at all | **Live-verified before and after, not assumed**: curled a real unauthenticated `/admin` visit and a real nonexistent path against a real running server both before the fix (headers genuinely absent) and after (present). `tests/Feature/Security/SecurityHeadersTest.php` (5 tests) |
| **Phase 14 specific — `X-Frame-Options: DENY` kept over the literal ask for `SAMEORIGIN`** | ✅ (deliberate, not an oversight) | `app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php` | This app never frames itself anywhere; `DENY` is strictly safer than `SAMEORIGIN` with zero functional cost, and matches the CSP's own `frame-ancestors 'none'`. Logged as a decision rather than silently complying with a downgrade that would have been a real regression |
| **Ad hoc — `BookingPolicy::viewAny()` no longer grants full admin booking-list access via `bookings.view_own`** | ✅ (fixed this task, was a real latent gap) | `app/Policies/BookingPolicy.php` (Decision #39) | Found while building the first-ever real caller of this policy method (`AdminBookingController`) — the old definition would have let any `staff`-role user (whose only permission is `bookings.view_own`) load every booking in the system, not just their own, the moment the new admin page shipped. `tests/Feature/Admin/AdminBookingControllerTest.php`'s first test proves a `staff` user gets a real `403` |
| **Ad hoc — `StaffTimeOff` ownership enforced server-side beyond the class-level Policy check** | ✅ (fixed this task) | `app/Http/Controllers/Admin/AvailabilityController.php::storeTimeOff()` | `StaffTimeOffPolicy::create()` intentionally allows any staff-linked user through at the class level (anticipating a future self-service request flow) with no model instance to check `staff_id` against — the controller adds an explicit `staff.manage` OR `staff_id === $user->staff->id` check so the shared admin page can't be used to add time off against a colleague's record. `tests/Feature/Admin/AvailabilityControllerTest.php` proves a staff member can add their own but gets a real `403` for a colleague's |
| **Phase 14 sub-step 2 — session cookie forced secure by default in production** | ✅ (fixed — was a real gap) | `config/session.php` — `'secure' => env('SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE', env('APP_ENV') === 'production')` | Previously a bare `env()` call with no production default — a deploy that forgot to set `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE` would silently ship session cookies over plain HTTP. `tests/Feature/Security/ProductionHardeningTest.php` proves the fallback expression resolves correctly for both environments, and that the current (non-production) value is still `false` |
| **Phase 14 sub-step 2 — trusted proxies + HTTPS scheme forcing for a reverse-proxy deployment** | ✅ | `bootstrap/app.php` — `$middleware->trustProxies(at: ...)`, env-driven via `TRUSTED_PROXIES`, empty (trust nothing) by default; `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php` — `URL::forceScheme('https')` gated on `app()->environment('production')` | Without this, a production deploy behind Nginx/a load balancer would see every request as insecure/from the proxy's own IP (breaking `$request->secure()`, the session secure-cookie flag above, and per-IP rate limiting alike) — a real gap that had never been exercised since no reverse-proxy environment has existed yet. `tests/Feature/Security/ProductionHardeningTest.php` proves a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` header is genuinely ignored with no trusted proxy configured (the current/default state) |
| **Phase 14 sub-step 2 — Excel formula-injection guard and server-side-price-only rows corrected** | ✅ (documentation fix, not new code) | See the corrected rows above (formula-injection, server-side pricing) | Both had shipped real, working implementations in earlier phases (6 and 7/12 respectively) but this checklist was never updated afterward — found and fixed while compiling the OWASP audit below, since a stale `⬜` next to an already-built control is itself a real audit-process finding |

### 9a. OWASP Top 10 (2021) Audit Matrix — Phase 14 sub-step 2

> Cross-references §9 above rather than duplicating its evidence — this table's job is coverage per
> OWASP category, not a second copy of every file:line citation. ✅ = real, verified mitigation in
> place. 🟡 = partial/mechanism exists but has a documented gap. N/A = the app genuinely has no
> attack surface for this category (stated explicitly, not silently skipped).

| # | Category | Status | Mitigation | Gap / Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A01 | Broken Access Control | ✅ | Route-level `role:super-admin\|admin\|receptionist\|staff` (`routes/admin.php`) + a real `Policy` class per model (32 models, `AllModelsHavePoliciesTest.php`) + per-action `->authorize()` calls in every controller. IDOR-scoped ownership checks (`BookingPolicy`, `CustomerProfilePolicy`, etc.) proven live via `IdorTest.php`. | Two real gaps in this exact category were found and fixed THIS sub-step (`BookingPolicy::viewAny()` over-granting via `bookings.view_own`; `StaffTimeOff` create-policy ownership) — evidence the control works when actually exercised, but also that it depends on catching gaps as new admin surfaces ship, not a one-time guarantee |
| A02 | Cryptographic Failures | ✅ | Argon2id password hashing + `Password::uncompromised()` breached-password check; encrypted PII casts (`guest_email`/`guest_phone`, `CustomerProfile.notes`, `two_factor_secret`/recovery codes); encrypted session cookies (`SESSION_ENCRYPT=true`); `spatie/laravel-backup` AES-256 backup encryption, live-verified (`encryption_method=259`). **This sub-step**: session cookie now forced `secure` by default in production, HTTPS scheme forcing + trusted-proxy configuration added (see §9 rows above) — closes the last real gap in this category (a production deploy without those would have shipped cleartext-capable session cookies despite everything else being encrypted) | None remaining known |
| A03 | Injection | ✅ | Eloquent/query-builder parameter binding everywhere; every raw SQL call site in the app uses `?` placeholders or a parameterless aggregate (`ServicesPreviewImport.php:45`, `ServiceImportController.php:157` — both `whereRaw('LOWER(name) = ?', [...])`; `DashboardController.php:54`, `PosRegisterController.php:182`, `ReportController.php:153` — all `selectRaw`/`DB::raw` with `SUM`/`DATE`, no interpolated user input). `SqlInjectionTest.php` proves a classic payload through both Eloquent and the real `/login` endpoint | None found |
| A04 | Insecure Design | ✅ | `BookingStateMachine` (a booking cannot skip statuses — enforced server-side, not just UI-hidden buttons); database-backed atomic slot holds (`slot_holds` table + `lockForUpdate()`, Decision #49) + a 3-layer double-booking guard (hold + DB `lockForUpdate()` + a status-aware unique index) — live-verified under 50 genuinely concurrent OS processes (Decision #30: 1 success, 49 clean rejections, 0 corruption); HMAC-signed price quotes so a tampered client total can never reach the database | None found |
| A05 | Security Misconfiguration | ✅ | `DebugModeGuard` fails closed (refuses to boot with `APP_DEBUG=true` in production); `SecurityHeaders` (CSP+nonce, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, HSTS) now genuinely present on every response including error pages (Phase 14 sub-step 1's fix); no source maps in the production build. Trusted-proxy configuration closes a real misconfiguration class specific to reverse-proxy deployments | — |
| A06 | Vulnerable and Outdated Components | ✅ | `composer audit`/`npm audit` both clean, wired into CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). **[2026-09-07 closed]** `.github/dependabot.yml` now exists — `composer`/`npm`/`github-actions`, weekly, grouped minor/patch updates (§10 #20) | — |
| A07 | Identification and Authentication Failures | ✅ | Fortify + Argon2id + breached-password check; mandatory TOTP 2FA for admin/super-admin/receptionist (`RequireTwoFactorAuthentication`); login/register/password-reset rate limiting + account lockout; session regeneration on login + logout-other-devices. The local-only `/admin/dev-login` 2FA-skip flag (this session's earlier ad hoc task) is double-gated (`app()->environment('local')` + a session flag only that one route sets) and route-registration-gated on top of that — confirmed absent outside local via `route:list` | None found in production-reachable code paths |
| A08 | Software and Data Integrity Failures | ✅ | CSRF (`ValidateCsrfToken` on the `web` group); HTML sanitization (`mews/purifier`) on rich text; secure upload pipeline (server-sniffed MIME + re-encode, strips EXIF/trailing payloads); Excel formula-injection guard (corrected row above — real, shipped since Phase 6); mass-assignment protection (`$fillable` everywhere + `preventSilentlyDiscardingAttributes`) | None found |
| A09 | Security Logging and Monitoring Failures | ✅ | `spatie/activitylog` on sensitive models (`User`/`Booking`/`Payment`/`Setting`) with actor/IP/user-agent/before-after diff, secrets excluded; `notification_logs` + an Audit Log viewer; a CSP-violation report endpoint (`/csp-report`). **This sub-step**: Sentry (`sentry/sentry-laravel`) installed and wired for real-time exception tracking with a PII scrubber — closes what was previously the one real hole in this category (an unhandled exception in production had nowhere to surface except server log files) | Frontend (browser-side JS) error tracking is NOT wired (§10 #21) — a React render crash or uncaught promise rejection still reports nowhere |
| A10 | Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) | N/A | Grepped the entire `app/` directory for any outbound HTTP call driven by user-controlled input (`Http::get/post`, `file_get_contents` on a variable, `curl_exec`) — the only match is `SecureUploadService.php:179` reading an already-uploaded file's own server-assigned temp path, not a user-supplied URL. No feature anywhere accepts a URL from a user and fetches it server-side (no webhook receiver, no "import from URL," no link-preview feature) | Revisit if such a feature is ever built — this is a genuine "no attack surface exists," not an unaudited gap |

## 11. Quick Reference

**One-time setup (already done on this machine)**
```bash
git init && git add . && git commit -m "..."      # done — see §13 for commit hashes
cp .env.example .env                              # done (Windows: copy .env.example .env)
"D:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysql.exe" -u root -e "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS looks_smart_salon CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;"
composer install --ignore-platform-req=ext-pcntl --ignore-platform-req=ext-posix
npm install
php artisan key:generate
php artisan migrate:fresh --seed --force   # now seeds a full realistic dataset (Phase 2) + roles/permissions (Phase 3)
```

**Seeded login credentials (all use password `password`)**
```
Super-admin:
  admin@lookssmartsalon.example
  NOTE: 2FA was confirmed on this account during the 2026-08-25 bugfix verification (real TOTP
  secret + recovery codes generated). It will NOT be forced through /two-factor-setup anymore. To
  test the forced-setup flow fresh, either re-seed (php artisan migrate:fresh --seed --force,
  wipes everything) or reset just this: UPDATE users SET two_factor_secret=NULL,
  two_factor_recovery_codes=NULL, two_factor_confirmed_at=NULL WHERE email='admin@lookssmartsalon.example';

Customers/staff: see the `users` table — emails are Faker-generated per seed run, e.g.
  SELECT email FROM users WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM staff) LIMIT 5;  -- customers
  SELECT u.email FROM users u JOIN staff s ON s.user_id = u.id LIMIT 5;        -- staff
```

**Local dev commands (native XAMPP — no Docker/Sail)**
```bash
npm run dev                   # Vite dev server (terminal 1)
php artisan serve             # Laravel app server (terminal 2)
php artisan inertia:start-ssr # SSR server (terminal 3, optional for local dev, required to test SSR)

# quality gates
php artisan test              # Pest
./vendor/bin/pint
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run format:check

# production-style build check
npm run build                 # client bundle → public/build
npm run build:ssr             # + SSR bundle → bootstrap/ssr (gitignored)
```

## 12. HANDOFF BLOCK — for handing the project to any other AI tool
> Copy this into the new tool (and attach all three .md files). Refresh it after every session.

```
I'm working on a Laravel 12 + Inertia v2 + React 19 (TypeScript) project: "Looks Smart Beauty Salon" —
a public booking website plus an admin management dashboard.

Attached files:
- 00-PROJECT-BRIEF.md  → tech stack, modules, security baseline, UI/SEO/performance standards (authoritative)
- 01-PHASE-PROMPTS.md  → the 14-phase build plan with the exact prompt for each phase
- 02-PROJECT-STATE.md  → what has been built so far, what remains, and which decisions were made

IMPORTANT ENVIRONMENT NOTES (deviate from the Brief — see Decisions #8-13):
- No Docker, no Laravel Sail. Local dev is native XAMPP: PHP 8.2.12, MariaDB 10.4.32, on Windows.
- Laravel 12 (not the Brief's stated 11) — Laravel is at v13 now; 12 is the PHP-8.2-compatible choice.
- **Redis was permanently removed from the project on 2026-09-30 (Decision #50).** Session/cache run
  on the `database` driver everywhere; queue is `sync` locally / `database` in staging-prod (Decision
  #49 migrated off Redis 2026-09-28 for RabHost Economy shared hosting, which has no Redis; Decision
  #50 then dropped the `predis/predis` and `laravel/horizon` packages, `config/horizon.php`, and all
  Redis config blocks entirely — nothing in the app depends on Redis anymore). Phase 3's session-handling
  code (`SessionsController::destroyOthers()`'s direct table delete, `LogSuccessfulLogin`'s IP lookup)
  runs against the `database` driver and has been verified live (§3 Phase 3) — no outstanding
  Redis-specific re-audit needed.
- Commands are `php artisan serve` + `npm run dev`, not `sail up`.
- Admin routes require auth+verified+2FA+role (Phase 3 + audit fix) AND real controllers now call
  `->authorize()` per action (`UserController`, `AuditLogController`, Phase 5) — see §10 #9, now
  substantially closed.
- No deposits and no prepaid packages in the schema — deliberate, see Decisions #19/#20 before adding either.
- Guests get passwordless magic-link booking access — BUILT (Phase 7 sub-step 5, Decision #21),
  live-verified against a real emailed link. `GuestBookingLinkGenerator`/`BookingManageController`.
- `laravel/passkeys` exists in composer.lock/migrations as an unused transitive dependency of Fortify
  — see Decision #23. Not a feature we're building.
- `@tanstack/react-table` was installed then removed (Phase 5 sub-step 2) — its published version is
  v9 with a substantially different API from the well-known v8; `DataTable` is hand-rolled instead.
  Don't reach for that package again assuming v8 semantics without re-checking its current API.
- **Laravel 11's event auto-discovery is ACTIVE — never also register a listener with
  `Event::listen()` if it already has a `handle()` method typed to the event.** Doing both silently
  double-fires it (found in Phase 7, Decision #32 — every login/lockout/notification event had been
  sent twice since Phase 3 before this was caught and fixed).
- **[Ad hoc task 39, 2026-09-25] `APP_URL` fixed to `http://127.0.0.1:8000`** (was `http://localhost`,
  no port) — the line above describing the OLD value is now stale/superseded. The missing port was one
  problem (signed URLs, §10 #24); a bigger one found this task: MediaLibrary builds every image URL
  from `APP_URL`, so a host mismatch (`localhost` vs. the `127.0.0.1` the admin actually browses)
  silently broke EVERY uploaded image site-wide via the CSP's `img-src 'self'` correctly blocking the
  cross-origin request. **Always keep `APP_URL` matching the exact host:port you browse to** — check
  this first if images stop rendering or a signed link 403s, before assuming a code bug.
- **Every admin form's Save button can be silently swallowed by `useUnsavedChangesGuard.ts` if that
  hook's `allowNextVisit()` escape hatch (added ad hoc task 39) is ever bypassed** — e.g. a new admin
  page that builds its own `<form>` instead of going through `ResourceForm.tsx`. The hook intercepts
  EVERY Inertia visit while a form is dirty, including the save's own `post()/put()` call; only
  `ResourceForm`'s `onSubmit` wrapper calling `allowNextVisit()` right before forwarding to the page's
  handler lets that specific visit through. Any new admin form must go through `ResourceForm`, not a
  bare `<form onSubmit={...}>`, or it will inherit this same silent-save-failure bug.
- **The public site now runs on the salon's REAL content, not placeholders** (content-sync +
  catalog-overhaul tasks, §4/§13). `database/seeders/SalonCatalogSeeder.php` holds the genuine
  catalog — **5 categories, 55 bookable services**, PKR prices; `DatabaseSeeder` no longer creates
  factory services/categories for the public catalog. Real address/phone/email/social/lat-long are
  seeded Settings, business hours are Mon-Sun 10:00-21:00. **If you add a service, put it in that
  seeder, not a factory.**
- **Every `base_price` in the catalog is ALREADY the 25%-discounted live price.** Do not apply a
  further discount anywhere, and do not add a runtime multiplier — `PriceQuoteService` computes every
  quote server-side from `base_price`, so a second implicit discount would silently disagree with the
  displayed price. To change the discount, edit the numbers in the seeder. The reasoning and the
  arithmetic proof are in that file's docblock.
- **Service imagery has a two-tier fallback.** A service's own uploaded medialibrary image wins; if
  it has none, `serviceData()` falls back to its category's `stock_image_url` (a remote Unsplash
  photo). That needs `https://images.unsplash.com` in the CSP's `img-src` — already there. When
  eager-loading a Service's category for anything that renders a card, select
  `category:id,name,stock_image_url`: a restricted `category:id,name` select silently returns a null
  image rather than erroring. Real photography uploaded via the admin Media Library supersedes stock
  automatically, no code change (§10 #40).
- **`app/Support/ServiceGuide.php` supplies the detail page's procedure/benefits/suitability/
  aftercare, keyed by TREATMENT FAMILY (SKU prefix), not per service and not by category.** Deliberate:
  55 bespoke clinical protocols would have meant fabricating specifics the salon never gave, on a page
  clients may follow after a chemical treatment. Family-keying is also more correct than category
  -keying — Short Hair Keratin Smoothing is filed under Spa/Specials but gets smoothing aftercare. If
  you add a service, give it an SKU whose prefix matches an existing family, or add a family.
- **The booking wizard reads `?service=<id>`** and preselects it, validating against the real services
  list. Every "Book now" link across the site depends on this; it was silently ignored before.
- **The homepage hero is a background video** (`public/images/looks smart beauty Salon in Lahore.mp4`,
  referenced via `encodeURI()` because the filename really does contain spaces). It needs no CSP
  change — there is no `media-src` directive so it inherits `default-src 'self'`, and the file is
  same-origin. The poster renders server-side and the `<video>` mounts **client-only** on purpose:
  React does not serialise `muted` into SSR HTML, and Chrome blocks autoplay on a server-rendered
  `<video autoplay>` that lacks it. Keep `video.muted = true` before `play()`, and keep the
  `.catch()` — `play()` genuinely rejects under data/battery saver.
- **Do NOT use framer-motion's `useReducedMotion()` to decide what to RENDER.** It is
  `useState(ref.current)` — a one-shot read that never updates (its own source says so), and under
  SSR that ref is `null`, so it locks in "motion allowed" forever and never corrects after
  hydration. It served the looping video to reduced-motion users until a browser test caught it. Use
  `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` with a change listener for render branching; the
  hook is only safe for animation config (which is all `PublicLayout` uses it for).
- **The public booking page is `/book`, NOT `/booking`.** Briefs have asked for `/booking` more than
  once; no such route exists (only `admin/bookings` and `api/booking/*`), so a link there 404s.
  Public routes are `/`, `/about`, `/services`, `/services/{slug}`, `/deals`, `/gallery`, `/blog`,
  `/blog/{slug}`, `/contact`, `/book`, `/privacy-policy`.
- **Opening hours live in `business_hours` and NOTHING may hardcode them.** Four surfaces render
  them — footer, homepage info band, About contact card, Contact sidebar — all through the same
  collapse logic (one line when the week is uniform, one line per distinct window otherwise). A
  brief has already asked for hardcoded hours that contradicted the database (11:00–8:30 vs the real
  10:00–21:00); read the rows instead and flag the discrepancy.
- **`posts.cover_image_path` (local upload, via `SecureUploadService`) and `posts.cover_image_url`
  (external — stock photo or `public/images/` asset) are TWO different columns with a defined
  precedence.** Always read the cover through `PublicWebsiteController::postCoverUrl()`, never
  either column directly — a real admin upload always wins, and the helper also makes a
  root-relative `cover_image_url` absolute (needed because `SeoHead` renders it straight into
  `og:image`, which social platforms require to be absolute). Mirrors `service_categories.
  stock_image_url`'s precedence pattern.
- **The blog's "Trending This Week" is most-recently-published, not real analytics.** This app
  tracks no page views or read counts anywhere. Do not wire it to anything that implies real
  traffic data without adding actual tracking first — the current label is deliberately honest
  about being a proxy, and `blog()`'s docblock says so explicitly.
- **`database/seeders/BlogContentSeeder.php` is where real blog content lives** — 7 categories
  (Hair, Skin Care, Facial, Bridal, Nails & Spa, Laser, Tips & Advice), 7 tags, 8 written articles.
  `DatabaseSeeder` no longer creates factory posts for the public blog. If you add an article, put
  it in that seeder's `articles()` list, not a factory — factory posts have no category, no tags and
  no HTML headings, which is exactly the gap this seeder was built to close.
- **Related-articles on a blog post tops up with other recent posts when its own category has fewer
  than 3** — a single-post category (Laser, at launch) would otherwise render an empty "Related
  articles" section. Keep this fallback if you add more categories; do not revert to a same-category-
  only query without checking every category still has ≥3 posts.
- **§10 #26 (two visual languages) is CLOSED as of ad hoc task 20.** `Gallery.tsx` (the last page)
  was rebuilt on theme tokens as part of its own category-sections redesign. Every public page is now
  on `ink`/`ivory`/`accent`/`font-display` — keep any new public page on that same convention.
- **`galleries.category` (a free-text string) no longer exists — it is `galleries.gallery_category_id`,
  a real FK into the new `gallery_categories` table (`app/Models/GalleryCategory.php`).** Categories
  now have their own admin-controlled `sort` (managed from the "Categories" card at the top of
  `/admin/gallery`, NOT the per-album `sort` column, which is a separate, older field). The public
  `/gallery` page groups ALL active albums' images by category and renders them as stacked sections in
  that `sort` order — a category with zero active images is simply not rendered; an active album with
  NO category assigned still has its images shown, under a trailing "More Highlights" section, rather
  than silently disappearing. If you touch gallery code and see a reference to `->category` as a plain
  string (an old test, a stale comment), it is wrong — fix it rather than trust it, the same lesson
  this task itself had to apply to a previously-missed `tests/Feature/BridalSliderTest.php` reference.
- **`/deals` is now a real, controller-backed page** (`PublicWebsiteController::deals()`, route name
  `deals.index`) — it is IN the sitemap and covered by `DealShowcaseTest.php`/`deals-page.spec.ts`.
  If you ever see a comment or test claiming `/deals` is "still the Phase 9 placeholder", it is stale;
  fix the comment/test rather than trusting it — this exact staleness was found and fixed in
  `SeoController.php`/`SeoControllerTest.php` during ad hoc task 14.
- **`database/seeders/DealShowcaseSeeder.php` is where real deal content lives** — 12 real package
  deals across all 6 `Deal::CATEGORY_TAGS`, each `original_price` the genuine sum of its bundled
  services' `base_price` and `deal_price` a real discount off that. `DatabaseSeeder` no longer creates
  factory deals for the public showcase; if you add a deal, put it in that seeder's `deals()` list,
  not a factory.
- **`Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection::only()`/`except()` filter by the model's PRIMARY KEY, NOT
  by the collection's array key.** `$collection->keyBy('sku')->only($someSkus)` silently returns an
  EMPTY collection with zero errors thrown anywhere — a real framework gotcha, found the hard way in
  `DealShowcaseSeeder`. If you ever need to filter a keyed `Eloquent\Collection` by its array keys,
  call `->toBase()` first to get a plain `Support\Collection`, whose `only()`/`except()` behave as
  documented.
- **`deals.image_path` holds EITHER a local `SecureUploadService` path OR a full external URL** —
  resolved via `PublicWebsiteController::dealImageUrl()`'s `str_starts_with($path, 'http')` check, the
  same precedent as `posts.cover_image_url`/`service_categories.stock_image_url`. Always read it
  through that helper, never the raw column.
- **`DealCarousel.tsx` uses real `scrollLeft`/`scrollBy()`, deliberately NOT `BridalMarquee.tsx`'s CSS
  `translateX` keyframe-animation pattern.** Do not "unify" the two carousels onto one shared
  component without re-reading `DealCarousel.tsx`'s own doc comment first — the divergence is
  intentional (deal cards have real interactive buttons a moving CSS transform would fight against,
  and the task's "manual navigation controls" requirement needs genuine deterministic scroll control).
- **No shared Media Library "select an existing upload" picker exists anywhere in this app** (§10
  #43). Every image field, Deal's included, only supports uploading a NEW file — there is nothing to
  wire a "select from library" button into yet.
- **The homepage's Google reviews are seeded/authored, not synced from a real Google API** (§10 #45)
  — there are no Google Places credentials anywhere in this project. `source = 'google'` on a
  `Review` row means "seeded to look like a Google review," not "verified against Google's live
  data." Don't build anything that treats these rows as ground truth for the salon's actual public
  Google rating.
- **`Review.customer_id` is NOT the only way to know who wrote a review anymore.** Always read
  `$review->display_name`/`$review->display_category` (accessors on the model), never
  `$review->customer?->name`/`$review->service?->category?->name` directly — a Google-sourced review
  has no `customer_id`/`service_id` at all and those direct reads would silently show nothing.
- **`ReviewsCarousel.tsx` reads `matchMedia('(min-width: 768px)')` in JS, not a CSS breakpoint, to
  decide 3-up vs. 1-up.** If the visible column count ever needs to change, change it in BOTH the
  component's `useVisibleCount()` hook and its `md:grid-cols-3` class — they must agree, since the
  auto-advance step size comes from the JS value alone.
- **`WriteReviewModal.tsx`'s submit action is now PURELY a local save — no external Google
  redirect, no clipboard write.** Task 16 briefly added a `window.open()`/`navigator.clipboard`
  step (working around Google not allowing pre-filled review text); task 17 removed that entirely
  on explicit instruction. Do not reintroduce either without a fresh, explicit ask — the
  `business.google_review_url` Setting that step depended on has also been deleted outright (schema
  entry, admin field, seeded row), not just unwired, so there is nothing left to silently resurrect.
- **`POST /reviews` (`PublicWebsiteController::submitReview()`) publishes immediately — no
  moderation queue.** This is deliberate (the task asked for instant carousel visibility), NOT an
  oversight matching `Admin\ReviewController`'s existing approve/reject flow for booking-linked
  organic reviews. If spam becomes a real problem, the fix belongs in the honeypot/time-trap/
  `throttle:review` layer (or adding real moderation here too), not in silently routing this
  endpoint's rows through the unrelated admin queue.
- **A guest's `name` on the Write a Review form is fully optional, defaulting to "Verified Guest"
  server-side** (`PublicWebsiteController::submitReview()`) when left blank — do not make it
  `required` again without checking why it was deliberately loosened (task 17, on explicit spec
  wording).
- **`Setting.value` is JSON-cast (`array`) — never `Setting::where(...)->update(['value' => $raw])`
  via the query builder.** That bypasses the cast and writes an un-encoded string into a JSON
  column, which threw a real `CONSTRAINT settings.value failed` error when tried live (found while
  updating `business.google_review_url`, since removed). Load the model and assign + `save()`
  instead, so the cast actually runs — relevant to any Setting write, not just the removed one.
- **The booking wizard (`Book.tsx`) has NO staff-selection step anymore, on purpose.** Do not add one
  back without re-reading why it was removed (ad hoc task 18) — `AvailabilityEngine` already resolves
  a real staff member per slot when `staff_id` is omitted from the availability request, and the
  chosen slot's own `staff_id` is what gets sent to `/api/booking/hold`/`/api/booking`. If a future
  task wants staff preference back, that's a deliberate UX decision to make again, not a bug to fix.
- **The 24h free-cancellation window check lives in ONE place now: `Booking::
  isWithinCancellationWindow()`.** `CancelBookingAction`, `RescheduleBookingAction`, and the customer
  -facing `CancelBookingDialog`'s fee-warning modal all read this exact same method (directly, or via
  `CustomerDashboardController::bookingData()`'s `within_cancellation_fee_window` field) — never
  reimplement the `now()->diffInHours(...)` check anywhere else, or the frontend's warning and the
  backend's actual accept/reject decision can silently drift apart again.
- **There is no monetary cancellation-fee/refund system anywhere in this codebase.** The
  `CancelBookingDialog`'s warning text is exactly that — a warning shown before an otherwise-normal
  cancellation call — not a payment/charge flow. Don't assume one exists when working on POS/payments
  code nearby.
- **`/my-bookings` (`Customer/Bookings.tsx`) and `/my-account`'s own "bookings" tab
  (`Customer/Profile.tsx`) both read from `CustomerDashboardController` but via 2 separate methods**
  (`bookings()` and `index()`) — if the booking-row shape ever needs a new field, add it to the
  shared private `bookingData()` helper once, not to one method's inline array.
- **Fortify's `/register` genuinely logs the account in and redirects to `/my-account`, but this can
  take several real seconds** (a verification email dispatches synchronously in this environment) —
  an e2e test waiting on that redirect needs a real navigation wait (`page.waitForURL('**/my-account')`),
  not a fixed short sleep. Also: the `register.store` rate limiter (`Limit::perMinutes(15, 5)` by IP,
  `AppServiceProvider`) is real and will genuinely 429 repeated test registrations from the same
  machine — `php artisan cache:clear` resets it in local dev if hit while iterating.
- **`Book.tsx`'s per-card "+ Add"/"Added" button carries a REAL, service-specific
  `aria-label={`${service.name}: ${isSelected ? 'Added' : 'Add'}`}`, not the bare visible word.** The
  card itself is a plain `<div>`, not a button — the Add button is the only interactive/pressable
  element per card. If you're writing a test or another component that needs to target a specific
  service's Add button, match on this label pattern (`/{name}: Add$/` / `/{name}: Added$/`), not the
  visible "Add"/"Added" text alone — a bare match will hit every card's button identically.
- **`PublicLayout`'s `AnimatePresence` exit-transition can re-render a page component AFTER Inertia's
  page store has already swapped to the destination page's props.** Any public page that reads its
  own page-specific props directly (`props.whatever`) without a fallback is at risk of the exact crash
  `Customer/Profile.tsx` hit on logout (fixed in task 19) if a user is ever navigated away from it —
  not just via a real logout, potentially any link click. When adding a new page with page-specific
  props, default them defensively (`props.thing ?? fallback`) rather than assuming they're always
  present, until/unless this layout's animation lifecycle itself gets a proper fix.
- **A 6th `ServiceCategory` named "Nails" exists in the dev database with 0 attached services** — not
  part of the original 5-category `SalonCatalogSeeder` catalog, origin not tracked down (found live
  while debugging a task-19 e2e failure). It's real, valid data (a category CAN legitimately have zero
  services), not a bug — but any future test clicking "the first real category pill" and assuming it
  has services should either check for this or iterate pills like `booking.spec.ts` now does.
- **`playwright.config.ts`'s global `timeout: 30_000` is not enough budget for a single e2e test that
  does multiple genuinely-slow real operations back to back** (registration + a multi-iteration
  date-search retry loop + a real booking + a cancellation, as `my-bookings.spec.ts` does) — this
  started genuinely timing out once real booking-slot contention grew with the suite itself (task 19).
  Scope a longer budget to the specific test with `test.setTimeout(N)` inside the test body rather than
  raising the global default for every test. Also: don't hardcode which real row is "newest"/"first"/
  "featured" in an e2e assertion against the live dev DB (`blog-pages.spec.ts` hardcoded the then-newest
  post's slug and broke the moment a genuinely newer post was added) — assert by shape instead
  (`/^\/blog\/[a-z0-9-]+$/`) when the test only needs to prove the link is real, not pin which content wins.
- **The contact form's contract**: `name`, `phone` (REQUIRED — the salon replies on WhatsApp),
  `email` (optional), `subject` (optional, folded onto `leads.notes`), `message`, plus the `website`
  honeypot and `rendered_at` time-trap. Do not reintroduce `service_interest`, and do not weaken
  the honeypot/time-trap — they return an identical success response to bots by design, so a
  "broken" silent submission may be that working correctly.
- **When rewriting a page, grep ALL of `tests/e2e` for that route, not just the spec named after
  it.** The About rebuild left `content-check.spec.ts` asserting four strings that no longer
  existed, and it was only caught a task later because that older spec also visits `/about`.
- **The Contact page was rebuilt on theme tokens** (ad hoc task 12) and asserts zero
  `indigo`/`purple`/`orange` classes. With About also converted, §10 #26's split is down to three
  pages: Blog, BlogDetail and Gallery. Its coordinate-pinned map lives in the location sidebar card
  and depends on the `frame-src https://www.google.com` CSP allowance.
- **The About page was rebuilt on theme tokens** (ad hoc task 11) and is asserted to contain zero
  `indigo`/`purple` classes, which removes one of the five pages behind §10 #26's two-visual-
  languages split. Its `about()` payload is now `quickStats` / `pillars` / `founder` / `contact` —
  the old `team` / `stats` / `timeline` / `values` props are gone, and the team roster is NOT to be
  restored until real staff records exist (it was publishing factory-generated names publicly).
- **Never substitute a stock or client photograph for a real person.** `founder.photo_url` is
  deliberately `null` and the card renders a monogram; the only portraits in the project are bridal
  *client* photos (§10 #42).
- **The homepage section order is a specified contract**, asserted by `tests/e2e/home-sequence.spec.ts`
  reading real document positions: Hero → Specialized Services → Deals/Offers → Why Choose Us
  (Our Legacy) → Gallery carousel → Client Reviews → WhatsApp QR → address/hours band → Footer.
  Inserting a section means updating that spec.
- **QR codes: use `App\Support\QrCode::svgDataUri()`.** It wraps `bacon/bacon-qr-code`, which is
  already present as a `laravel/fortify` dependency — do NOT add a QR package or call an external QR
  service (`img-src` is `'self' data: https://images.unsplash.com`, so a remote QR image is blocked,
  and it would leak the encoded contents). It returns a base64 `data:` URI specifically so the page
  can use a plain `<img src>` instead of `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
- **The WhatsApp number, chat link and QR all derive from the one `business.phone` setting.** Change
  it in admin Settings and all three update together; never hardcode a `wa.me` URL alongside it.
- **`#25D366` (WhatsApp green) is the only hardcoded colour allowed on the public site.** Everything
  else uses the theme tokens (`ink`, `ivory`, `surface`, `border-soft`, `accent-50…700`) and the
  `font-display` (Fraunces) / `font-sans` (Inter) families. The reference screenshots the salon
  supplies are coral-themed — deliberately NOT copied.
- **The homepage's "Why Trust" stat figures are editorial marketing claims, not computed values**
  (`PublicWebsiteController::legacyStats()`), and they knowingly disagree with the About page's
  live-computed stat band — see §10 #41 before "fixing" either side.
- **The homepage bridal marquee is CSS-only, and must stay that way.** `.marquee-*` rules live in
  `resources/css/app.css`; everything dynamic is a DATA ATTRIBUTE (`data-count` picks the duration,
  `data-paused` pauses during a drag). Do NOT reach for framer-motion or an inline
  `--marquee-duration` here — `style-src` has no `unsafe-inline` and inline styles are already being
  blocked on public pages (§10 #39). The loop works by rendering the list twice and translating
  `-50%`; the second pass is `aria-hidden`, so keep them in sync if you change the markup. Duration
  classes are enumerated for 2-12 images — **add a rule if the salon ever enables more than 12**, or
  it silently falls back to the 30s default.
- **Any new CSS animation needs an explicit `prefers-reduced-motion` escape.** `app.css` has a
  blanket `animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important`, which
  does not "disable" a keyframe animation so much as **run it to completion instantly** — for the
  marquee that parked the track at `translateX(-50%)`, visibly broken. Cancel `animation`/`transform`
  outright for anything whose end state is not its resting state.
- **Playwright's `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` option does NOT work** on @playwright/test 1.62.1 here
  (verified at both describe and file level — `matchMedia(...).matches` came back false). It made one
  test pass for the wrong reason. Emulate over CDP instead:
  `(await page.context().newCDPSession(page)).send('Emulation.setEmulatedMedia', { features: [{ name: 'prefers-reduced-motion', value: 'reduce' }] })`.
  Also remember `locator.count()` does not auto-wait — assert something visible first, or you will
  count a pre-hydration DOM.
- **Homepage slider images: `gallery_images.show_on_homepage`, ordered by album `sort` then image
  `sort`.** That is deliberate — the existing reorder arrows double as slider priority, so there is
  no `homepage_sort` column and no second reorder UI. Resolution lives in
  `App\Support\FeaturedGalleryImages` (curated first, else `public/images/` via
  `PublicImageScanner` — a fallback, never a blend). Only images in an ACTIVE album qualify.
- **`php artisan storage:link` is required on a fresh clone** and had never been run on this machine
  — without it every `asset("storage/…")` URL (all gallery and slider imagery, service uploads,
  logos) 404s while looking perfectly correct in the markup.
- **The homepage's "Our Specialized Services" pills come from the `categories` prop**, never a
  hardcoded list — a literal array is exactly what drifted when the catalog was replaced. `home()`
  therefore fetches 8 services per category (featured first) rather than 6 featured overall, or most
  pills would filter down to an empty grid. **Staff working hours and business hours share `DatabaseSeeder`'s
  `OPENING_TIME`/`CLOSING_TIME` constants on purpose** — `AvailabilityEngine` intersects the two, so
  changing one alone silently publishes hours that cannot be booked.
- **The footer reads a globally shared Inertia prop called `site`, NOT `business`.** The name matters:
  Contact and PrivacyPolicy each pass their own page-level `business` prop, and Inertia merges page
  props over shared props SHALLOWLY — naming the shared one `business` made the page prop replace it
  entirely and crashed the footer client-side. Don't rename it back, and don't add a page prop called
  `site`. Contact details/hours in the footer are never hardcoded; the collapsed hours summary is
  cached under the `business:hours-summary` key and invalidated by
  `SettingController::updateHours()`.
- **CSP `frame-src` allows `https://www.google.com`** so the Contact page's maps embed can render; it
  was `'none'`, which had silently blocked that iframe since Phase 9. `frame-ancestors 'none'` is
  unchanged — the relaxation is outbound only. **`style-src` still has no `unsafe-inline`, which
  silently blocks Framer Motion's runtime inline styles on every public page** — a real, pre-existing
  gap against Brief §6's motion requirement, logged as §10 #39 with three concrete options. Expect
  `"Applying inline style violates..."` console errors in a browser; they are known, not new.
- **`lucide-react` v1.x has NO brand icons** — importing `Facebook`/`Instagram` from it is a hard
  TypeScript error. Use `resources/js/Components/SocialIcons.tsx` (local inline SVG, lucide-matching
  geometry). Don't add a second icon package for these.
- **Currency is PKR, not USD** (Decision #37) — `resources/js/lib/currency.ts` / `app/Support/
  CurrencyFormatter.php` are the ONLY places that should ever format a money value for display
  (`Rs. 2,500`, 0 decimals by default). Never add a new local `Intl.NumberFormat(...)` in a page —
  that's exactly the duplication that let 23 real hardcoded-currency spots accumulate before this was
  centralized. `business.currency` Setting is `PKR`.
- **Never call `app()->environment()` (or anything else touching the container) directly inside a
  config file's returned array** (Decisions #41/#42) — config files load during `artisan
  package:discover`'s minimal bootstrap (Composer's `post-autoload-dump` script), which runs BEFORE
  the container's `env` binding exists; doing so crashes every `composer require`/`install` with
  `"Target class [env] does not exist"`. Read the raw env var directly instead (`env('APP_ENV') ===
  'production'`). Same idea for closures in config values — `artisan config:cache` `var_export()`s
  everything, which cannot serialize a `Closure`; use a `[ClassName::class, 'method']` array callable
  instead (see `config/sentry.php`'s `before_send`). A service provider's `boot()` method does NOT
  have this problem — it runs much later in the lifecycle, after environment detection.
- `composer.json`'s `config.platform` pins `ext-pcntl`/`ext-posix` to a fake version (Decision #40) —
  needed only because `laravel/horizon` requires both and Windows has neither; this is a Windows-dev-
  machine-only workaround. A real Linux deploy target doesn't need it (both extensions genuinely exist
  there) but the override is harmless to leave in place either way.
- Sentry is installed on BOTH sides now, both inert with no DSN set (same pattern as Twilio/Google
  Calendar): backend `sentry/sentry-laravel` (`SENTRY_LARAVEL_DSN`), frontend `@sentry/react@10.73.0`
  wired into `resources/js/app.tsx` (module-scope `Sentry.init()`, gated on `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` +
  `VITE_APP_ENV === 'production'`) and `ErrorBoundary.tsx`'s `componentDidCatch` — see §10 #21 (closed).
- **Backup restore is now genuinely rehearsed, not just created.** `php artisan backup:restore-rehearsal`
  (`app/Console/Commands/BackupRestoreRehearsalCommand.php`) restores the latest real backup zip into a
  disposable `{db}_restore_rehearsal` scratch database (never the real one) and row-count-verifies it —
  run for real 2026-09-07, PASS on all 5 checked tables. See §10 #19 (closed).
- **`.github/dependabot.yml` now exists** — composer/npm/github-actions, weekly. See §10 #20 (closed).
- **Playwright E2E now exists** (`playwright.config.ts`, `tests/e2e/`) — run with `npx playwright test`
  (Chromium+WebKit) or `npx playwright test --project=chromium` for a fast/fully-reliable run.
  `webServer` auto-starts `php artisan serve`, reusing one already running locally. **Real, previously
  -shipped production bug found this way**: `Book.tsx`'s `submit()` used to collide with its own
  wizard-level Redis hold when calling `CreateBookingAction` — fixed (see §4). **WebKit is reliable
  individually but flaky in longer sequential runs on this machine** — `php artisan serve` is
  structurally single-threaded on Windows (no `pcntl_fork()` for `PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS` — Decision
  #30), not a code defect; prefer `--project=chromium` for a fast, always-reliable check, and treat a
  WebKit failure as suspect-environment-first, not suspect-app-first, unless it reproduces identically
  more than once. If Playwright's dev server gets stuck/stale after many manual runs, kill the
  `php.exe` holding port 8000 before the next run (`reuseExistingServer` will otherwise keep reusing
  a degraded long-lived process indefinitely).

Fixed in two parts: `bootstrap/app.php` now `prepend`s `SecurityHeaders` instead of `append`ing it, and `SecurityHeaders::handle()` wraps `$next($request)` in a `try/catch`, rendering the exception through the app's own `ExceptionHandler` (with an explicit `report()` call, since the kernel's own automatic one only fires for exceptions that reach ITS catch block, not one swallowed here) so the response still passes through the header-application code below. Both the broken and fixed states were curled live, not just tested. Also removed one genuinely unreachable dead-code branch in the same exception handler (a `$status === 500` check that could never be reached, since status 500 was already unconditionally handled by the guard above it) — confirmed via code reading that `Errors/500.tsx` renders the same generic message either way, so this was a clarification, not a behavior change. (2) The Sentry `before_send` scrubber's first version was an inline closure, which broke `artisan config:cache` outright (`LogicException`: a `Closure` can't be `var_export()`-ed) — caught by the PRE-EXISTING `DebugModeGuardTest`'s own config-cache regression test failing, not a new test; fixed by extracting the scrubber to a static method reference, `App\Support\SentryPiiScrubber::scrub()` (Decision #42). Also hit and fixed an unrelated Windows-only Composer platform-requirement landmine along the way — `laravel/horizon` requires `ext-pcntl`/`ext-posix`, genuinely Unix-only extensions that don't exist on Windows at all — via a `composer.json` `config.platform` override (Decision #40); latent since Phase 1, only surfaced now because `composer require`'s fresh dependency resolution re-validates platform requirements in a way `composer install` from an existing lock file doesn't. **Also corrected 2 stale §9 checklist rows found while compiling the audit, a real audit-process finding in its own right**: the Excel formula-injection guard (shipped since Phase 6 sub-step 4) and server-side-price-only computation (shipped since Phase 7/12) had both been left marked `⬜ Pending` long after the real implementations existed.
